name: Akwe:kon
category: Housing and Residence Life - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential
description: Akwe:kon (pronounced uh-GWAY-go) opened its doors in 1991, making it the nation's first university residence hall established to celebrate American Indian culture and heritage. In the Mohawk language, Akwe:kon means "all of us," reflecting the spirit of inclusiveness the house offers to students and the broader community. Akwe:kon's 35 residents represent diverse cultures and backgrounds; roughly half are Native American. Whatever their cultural background or tribal nationality, residents share an interest in past and contemporary Native issues and the importance of community and extended family. Situated on Cornell's north campus, Akwe:kon's distinctive building and landscape were designed with extensive input from Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) people, incorporating symbols that reflect the theme of communal spirit. Akwe:kon's presence on campus goes beyond the beauty of its structure, and includes activities and events that provide its residents and the entire Cornell community with ways to experience aspects of American Indian cultures and traditions. Throughout the year, Akwe:kon – in conjunction with the American Indian and Indigenous Studies Program (AIISP)– sponsors activities and programs featuring art, dances, film screenings, lectures, music, traditional foods, workshops and much more. Events are open to the public, and enable the whole Cornell community to experience the spirit of Native cultures and traditions.

category: Housing and Residence Life - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential
description: The LLC has, and will continue to, build socially conscious and community-minded individuals. Our goals have been, and still are, t0 provide knowledge of our culture and the problems facing Latinxs so that the future leaders of our communities will be prepared with the skills and sensitivity necessary to effect social change. The LLC has aimed to attract more Latinx students to Cornell University, thus enabling more students to complete academic programs. Through a philosophy of openness and inclusiveness, the LLC moved forward increasing student leadership and support, multicultural competency, and awareness of the spectrum of Latinx cultures. By combining the values in the LLC Common Bond and H&RL Programmatic Learning Objectives they will ideally act as a guide for the actions and decisions of individuals as they interact with and support each other, as well as other communities on campus. This extends to the both in and out of house members of the LLC and affiliated students, staff, and faculty. We are not just members of these communities, but representatives as well.

description: Welcome to the Mews Hall and Loving House: the LGBTQ+ Living Learning Unit community page! Mews Hall is home to over 200 first-year students and Loving House consists of 30 students from all class years. Our community is located on North Campus, conveniently located next to the Appel Commons, Robert Purcell Community Center and the Helen Newman Gym. The Mews community is committed to providing a high quality living learning experience that allows residents to learn about self and community through opportunities for engagement and leadership. The community is supported by a staff who is trained to help you get acclimated to the Cornell environment, provide ongoing support, and offer fun and educational programs throughout the academic year. Our staff includes 9 Resident Advisors (RAs), a Senior Resident Advisor (SRA) and a Residence Hall Director (RHD). In addition to the many hall-wide programs we offer throughout the year, we have a Residence Hall Leadership Organization, supported through the Residential Student Congress (RSC), known as the Mews Community Council. Residents will have the opportunity to serve as representatives for their floors and overall Mews and Loving House Community as well as have the opportunity to run for executive positions within the council. We welcome you to going us in these and other amazing opportunities in Mews.

name: Alpha Chi Omega
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Alpha Chi Omega was founded at DePauw University in Greencastle, Indiana on October 15, 1885. Its seven founders, who were all music students, sought "friendship, artistic society and advancement of the 'principles of true womanhood.'" Today, Alpha Chi Omega has over 200,000 members nationally with over 135 collegiate chapters and 200 alumnae chapters. The Zeta Phi chapter of Alpha Chi Omega was founded at Cornell in 1984 with 55 women. In the past thirty years, the Zeta Phi chapter has flourished from a small group of women meeting in classrooms to recognition as one of the strongest sororities on Cornell's campus - an organization in which academic excellence, community involvement, and leadership are exemplified through its 150 members. The Zeta Phi chapter is the oldest of the four Ivy League chapters of Alpha Chi Omega.

category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek

name: Alpha Epsilon Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Alpha Epsilon Phi was founded on October 24th, 1909 by seven young women at Barnard College. Our mission is to to inspire and support exemplary women dedicated to friendship and a lifelong commitment to Alpha Epsilon Phi while building on the vision of our Jewish founders. The Kappa Chapter of Alpha Epsilon Phi sorority was founded on Cornell's campus in 1920. AEPhi's national motto is "Many Hearts, One Purpose", and this rings true here at Cornell. Our sisterhood is comprised of women with a wide range of backgrounds, interests and aspirations. Our organization values scholarship, service and philanthropy, in addition to sisterhood and leadership development in each of our members. We pride ourselves on our diverse sisterhood and each sister's contribution to our chapter and the greater Cornell community.

name: Alpha Gamma Rho
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: The Beginnings of Alpha Gamma Rho start in 1912 with the foundation of the Caduceus chapter at Cornell University. The founders were a close knit group of men dedicated to issues concerning agriculture. On December 19, 1914, Caduceus received a charter from Alpha Gamma Rho national and has Zeta Chapter ever since. The first AGR house sat at 409 Dryden Ave until 1916 when a new house was built at 203 Highland Ave, the present location of the house. Since 1914, Alpha Gamma Rho has been the home to over 1700 men. Alpha Gamma Rho (AGR) is the national agricultural fraternity, with sixty two chapters across the United States. AGR boasts a rich tradition of close brotherhood, good times, and prides itself on its reputation of being a friendly fraternity. For over seventy years, Cornell's Zeta chapter has been the home for over 1800 members who have gone on to become leaders in many diverse fields. We feel that AGR is a close knit group of individuals because many of our brothers are closely associated with agriculture, which allows us to form incredibly strong bonds of friendship unparalleled in many fraternity experiences. However, a surprising number of our brothers are not from agricultural backgrounds, which contributes to our amazing diversity. Brothers of Alpha Gamma Rho are also extremely busy with organizations outside of the house such as philanthropies and community service, varsity and intramural sports, as well as the Cornell Inter-fraternity Council. Whether it means holding social events, or just hanging out together, we form friendships that last forever. In a place as big as Cornell University, it's nice to have a place to call home, a place where we call each other brothers and friends, and a place that makes our college years some of the most rewarding years of our lives. For us, we call this place Alpha Gamma Rho. Purpose: To Make Better Men, and through them a broader and better agriculture by surrounding members with influences tending to encourage individual endeavor, resourcefulness, and aggressive effort along lines making for the development of better mental, social, moral, and physical qualities; to promote a wider acquaintance and a broader outlook on the part of agricultural men through fellowship in a national organization that stands for the best social, mental, and moral development.

name: Alpha Kappa Alpha
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated is an internationally recognized sorority that was founded on the campus of Howard University on January 15th, 1908. Our sorority has since flourished to serve communities all across the world and is now comprised of over 390,000 members. Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated aims to cultivate and encourage high scholastic and ethical standards, to promote unity and friendship among college women, to study and help alleviate problems concerning girls and women in order to improve their social stature, to maintain a progressive interest in college life, and to be of Service to All Mankind. The Mu Upsilon Chapter of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated was chartered on March 31st, 1979, on the campus of Cornell University to foster sisterhood on this campus and to serve Cornell students, the Greater Ithaca Community, and All Mankind.

name: alpha Kappa Delta Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: The sisterhood of alpha Kappa Delta Phi provides women with a sense of belonging that nurtures life-long friendships, develops self-empowered leaders, and strengthens communities through service, scholarship, and Asian-Awareness.

name: Alpha Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Alpha Phi was the first American college sorority. It was founded at Syracuse University in 1872, where Alpha Chapter still exists. At its formation the sisterhood numbered ten women. One of these was Martha Foote Crowe, who later became Alpha Phi's first president. "Pursuing their studies in a thoroughly male-dominated environment, these women had a pressing need for friends who could sympathize with each other's problems and support each other's aspirations."(The Ivy Leaf) In addition, Alpha Phi organized the first interfraternity association, known today as the National Panhellenic Conference, in 1902 when they called the first successful inter-sorority meeting with Pi Beta Phi, Kappa Alpha Theta, Kappa Kappa Gamma, Delta Gamma, Gamma Phi Beta, and Delta Delta Delta. Alpha Phi is now an international fraternity having over 140 chapters throughout the United States and Canada. Alpha Phi has a membership of over 100,000 women and approximately 4,500 women pledge Alpha Phi every year. Objective/Aim of Sorority: At all times, it is our aim to consciously endeavor to promote the highest ideals of womanhood. In our effort to become more effective and contributing members of society, we shall strive for growth of character, intellectual development and excellence of scholarship, as well as to perfect our leadership capabilities. In all that we do, we shall encourage unity of feeling, sisterly affection, and social communion. We shall employ the principles of justice and right and give and receive mutual criticism in a spirit of love. As we search for truth and individual growth, we shall be mindful of our personal conduct. Our attitudes, beliefs and actions must in no way reflect a damaging influence on the image of our Chapter or Fraternity, or our sisters individually. We shall endeavor to represent the best in culture and refinement. We shall abide by the Constitution, Standing Rules and Collegiate Chapter Operations Manual of Alpha Phi International Fraternity. Specifically, we wish to instill and preserve individual integrity and excellence of personals standards befitting an Alpha Phi. (Taken from Collegiate Chapter Operations Manual) Cornell Chapter History: Delta Chapter's history begins with a visit by two Syracuse Alpha Phis in early 1889 for the purpose of beginning a chapter at Cornell. These visitors pledged four Cornell women who then pledged five more. In February 1889, Alpha initiated these nine women in a ceremony held at the Ithaca Hotel. Delta Chapter has been located in a number of places during its years of existence. First housed in Sage College, the chapter moved there in 1898. A house unit was tried from 1907-8 at 214 Eddy Street but failed as the sisters felt they lost interest in University affairs. The chapter remained in Sage College until 1917 when a shortage of housing forced University officials to request that organized groups find their own houses. Delta rented Alpha Zeta's house at 214 Thurston Ave. for the year 1917-8. 1918-1921 were spent at 114 Kelvin Place. In 1921, this house was sold necessitating a move. 411 Thurston, a house built by Amy Cooper Wurster (Alpha '91) was purchased and has remained the chapter house ever since. The original house, pictures of which may be seen in old Cornelians, was enlarged twice. Once in 1937, when the side wings were added and again in 1961, when the new wing was built. Philanthropy: Since 1946, Alpha Phi has focused on heart disease and cardiac care as a philanthropic priority. Today, research into the diagnosis and treatment of women's heart disease in a special interest of the Alpha Phi Foundation. Gender differences in diagnosing and treating cardiac health problems are becoming widely recognized, and donors can make a difference for thousands of women through gifts to the Alpha Phi Foundation. The Foundation funds educational programming in the areas of alcohol and AIDS awareness, women's health and safety, and other Watch Care programs developed for Alpha Phi collegiate chapters. The Foundation also funds the educational training sessions at Convention and Leadership Conferences that help officers develop the skills necessary to assume strong leadership roles within their chapters, as well as in the future. Participants in Convention and Leadership Conferences learn new insights into building effective teams and improving relationships, which they, in turn, use to enhance their chapters. The Foundation also supports women in all stages of their education. Undergraduate and graduate scholarships are awarded to Alpha Phi collegians and alumnae every year. Nontraditional educational scholarships are also available to Alpha Phi women who need additional course work for certification, career advancement or to reenter the work force.

name: Alpha Phi Alpha
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Alpha Phi Alpha, the first intercollegiate Greek-letter fraternity established for African American Men, was founded at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York by seven college men who recognized the need for a strong bond of brotherhood among African descendants in this country. The visionary founders, known as the "Jewels" of the fraternity, are Henry Arthur Callis, Charles Henry Chapman, Eugene Kinckle Jones, George Biddle Kelley, Nathaniel Allison Murray, Robert Harold Ogle, and Vertner Woodson Tandy.

name: Alpha Sigma Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Iota Chapter at Cornell was founded on March 27, 1909, by a group of ten undergraduates. The new fraternity prospered, and in 1913 it moved to its current location teetering over the edge of Fall Creek Gorge. The west wing containing 15 single rooms and the north wing, with expanded dining and social facilities, were added in 1924. Major improvements have been made to Rockledge Estate regularly. Alpha Sig has made and continues to make distinctive contributions to the Cornell community. Andrew Dickson White, the first president of and co-founder of Cornell, was initiated into the fraternity at Yale in 1850. He served as the fraternity's national president from 1913 to 1915 and helped found the chapter at Cornell. Other distinctive alumni include past and current deans of the Agriculture, Hotel, and Veterinary colleges at Cornell, and presidents of major corporate firms.

name: Alpha Xi Delta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Alpha Xi Delta was founded in 1893 by ten young women at Lombard College, Galesburg, Illinois, who shared a vision and a dream of a national organization dedicated to the personal growth of women. One of the oldest women's fraternities, Alpha Xi Delta is proud of its rich history. As one of the ten founding fraternities of the National Panhellenic Conference, it was Alpha Xi Delta's first NPC Chairman who wrote the Panhellenic Creed, which is still recited on college campuses today. Since that time more than a 100 years ago, the spirit of Alpha Xi Delta has enriched the lives of thousands of women throughout the world with its emphasis on lifelong learning and lasting friendship. Now a national fraternity with more than 120,000 initiated members, Alpha Xi Delta has grown into a progressive and forward-thinking organization with college chapters and alumnae associations throughout the United States. The ideals envisioned by our Founders are timeless and have remained constant throughout the years, inspiring pride in each member to pursue individual excellence. Our Founders left us a great legacy--they taught us the value of education because it would free us to achieve our goals and give us the power to be whatever we choose to be. They taught us to support one another through shared experiences and understanding. They taught us to serve others--to reach out to those less fortunate to make their lives better. It is these ideals of personal development, scholarship, friendship, and civic responsibility that we embrace and bring to every Alpha Xi Delta member.

name: Beta Theta Pi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Beta Theta Pi is devoted to developing Men of Principle for a principled life. The Cornell Chapter of Beta Theta Pi began in 1879 and has maintained an uninterrupted presence at Cornell University ever since. The Beta Delta chapter has produced many notable graduates including Adolph Coors Jr '09, Carl A. Kroch '35, Gustavo Vollmer '42, Jon Lindseth '56, and David Duffield '62.

name: Chi Psi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Chi Psi is a Fraternity of gentlemen that strive to pursue excellence in every facet of our daily lives.

name: Delta Chi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Delta Chi was founded as a law fraternity on October 13th, 1890 at Cornell University. In 1922, a collective body of members decided to register Delta Chi as a general fraternity, thereby opening membership to men of any academic discipline. In 1929, Delta Chi became the first fraternity to abolish the hazing practices associated with "hell week." Since that time, Delta Chi has evolved into an international organization, now including 120 chapters and colonies, and over 90,000 members worldwide.

name: Delta Delta Delta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Delta Delta Delta Fraternity, founded in 1888 at Boston University, began as an organization concerned with the growth and development of college women and has evolved into a leader among sororities. The Alpha Beta Chapter was founded at Cornell University in 1913 and celebrates nearly 100 years of history in Ithaca, New York. Beginning with only a handful of members in 1913, the Alpha Beta Chapter now boasts over 130 active collegiate members, as well as a strong alumnae presence. Among the active members there are many leaders, academic achievements to record, and many inspirational examples of personal growth. Most importantly, in the Alpha Beta Chapter, each sister is guided by and promises to live in accordance with Delta Delta Delta's national motto of sisterhood: "Let Us Steadfastly Love One Another."

name: Delta Gamma
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Delta Gamma offers to women of all ages a rich heritage based on principles of personal integrity, personal responsibility and intellectual honesty. Its primary purpose is to foster high ideals of friendship, promote educational and cultural interests, create a true sense of social responsibility, and develop the finest qualities of character. Our chapter is made up of over 125 incredibly talented, diverse, and intelligent women, and every unique woman serves as an inspiration to me on a daily basis. Cornell Delta Gammas are involved all over campus. From writing for the Cornell Daily Sun, to competing on varsity sports teams and holding leadership positions throughout the Cornell community, our sisters are extremely active on Cornell's campus. It is no surprise that Cornell Delta Gammas obtain some of the most competitive jobs and internships every year. Despite how busy we all are, one common thread that links us all is our passion to "do good." This is our motto, and we accomplish this every year through our service initiatives. Our members give their time and talent to raise money for our philanthropy, Service for Sight. Through these efforts, as well as throughout our daily lives, we fulfill our primary purpose, set by our founders in 1873: "We encourage an atmosphere which will foster high ideals of friendship among college women, promote their educational and cultural interests, create in them a true sense of social responsibility and develop in them the best qualities of character."

name: Delta Kappa Epsilon
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: DKE strives to develop a culture and an expectation of​ undergraduate​ chapters who perform in the top tier of fraternities at their institutions​;​ and a vibrant network of ​alumni who are motivated to stay involved with the fraternity after graduation. We will do this by providing our undergraduates with the leadership​ skills, and the operational resources they need, to excel in today’s Greek environment; and by developing alumni networking programs which are relevant and engaging, and are beneficial to both alumni and undergraduates.

name: Delta Sigma Theta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is a public service organization of college educated women committed to the development of its members and uplifting the community. The Magnificent Mu Gamma Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated was charted on May 4, 1975. Our chapter members strive to carry on the legacy of our beautiful founders and the thousands of women who came before us through sisterhood, scholarship and service.

name: Delta Upsilon
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Delta Upsilon is the premier men's fraternity committed to Building Better Men for a global society through service, leadership development and lifelong personal growth for our diverse membership.

name: Kappa Alpha Psi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: This fraternity strives to unite college men of culture, patriotism, and honor in a bond of fraternity; to encourage honorable achievement in every field of human endeavor; to promote the spiritual, social, intellectual, and moral welfare of its members; to assist the aims of colleges and universities; and to inspire service in the public interest.

name: Kappa Alpha Theta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Kappa Alpha Theta was founded at Cornell in 1881 and was the first female fraternity. Iota left the Cornell campus in 1965 after a policy disagreement with the Kappa Alpha Theta headquarters' administration. In 1980, Iota returned to Cornell as the national office realized the demand for a chapter at Cornell. One of Iota's most famous alumnae is Anna Botsford Comstock, for which Comstock Hall is named after.

name: Kappa Delta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: The Omega Chi Chapter of Kappa Delta received its charter in the spring of 1917, becoming the 21st chapter in the national sorority. In 1928, Kappa Delta moved into its first house and current residence at 109 Triphammer Rd. KD is one of three Cornell sororities that still owns its original property. The Omega Chi Chapter of Kappa Delta left Cornell's campus on October 21, 1969 when the entire house deactivated in protest of KD national's refusal to allow Jewish sisters as members. The house was reinstated in May of 1975 after a change in Kappa Delta policy. Today, the Omega Chi Chapter of Kappa Delta is thriving at Cornell. We are an organization of over 150 diverse, intelligent, talented and strong women. We know that our chapter has helped Kappa Delta become something far beyond what even the Founders dreamed.

name: Kappa Delta Rho
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: On May 24, 1913, Harold A. Severy, an alumnus of the Middlebury chapter doing graduate study here at Cornell University, founded KDR's second chapter. The original twenty-three members of Beta chapter made their home at the local YMCA, and the chapter remained active until the first World War, when it closed temporarily. Beta chapter was refounded in 1920 and moved to 306 Highland Road (next door to our present address). The house continued to grow throughout the 1920s and was a strong athletic fraternity during the 1930s, winning, perhaps for the last time in history, Cornell's all-sports trophy in 1935. The chapter closed again (as did all Kappa Delta Rho chapters) for the second World War, and was refounded by local alumni in the spring of 1950. In 1952 we moved into our current address at 312 Highland Road, and in 1964, a new wing including a kitchen, a dining room, and several new study rooms was added to keep up with the increasing needs of the brotherhood. The house itself has an interesting history as well. It was built in 1909 as an experiment by Cornell University's architecture school - all the outside walls of the original structure are made entirely of poured cement.

name: Kappa Kappa Gamma
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: In the fall of 1883, five women at Cornell University applied to Kappa Kappa Gamma for a charter and became Psi chapter three weeks later. They joined a strong and successful Greek system which was stated by a Psi historian to be "deeply imbedded in Cornell, both for men and women." In 1921, the chapter raised enough funds to buy a house at 508 Thurston Avenue which is still the same location of the sorority house today. Since the beginning days, Psi chapter has upheld very high ideals, both for themselves and for their community. In 1961, the Dean of Students said of Psi, "The women of Psi chapter of Kappa Kappa Gamma have made the Panhellenic Creed a living reality on our campus and the student community has profited from their positive leadership." This leadership continues today as evidenced by the many Greek awards and recognition that Psi chapter receives each year. The women of Psi chapter have also taken their leadership skills beyond college with their extensive amount of Kappa Achievement Alumnae Awards. Each year, during spring rush, it has been the hope of every sister that new pledges are chosen that will be as faithful and enthusiastic to carry out the ideals of Psi chapter that were established in 1883 and since upheld.

name: Kappa Phi Lambda
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: We, the sisters of the Kappa Phi Lambda Sorority strive to strengthen sisterhood amongst women by providing service and promoting cultural diversity to our members and our community, thus securing the bond of kinship for posterity. Kappa Phi Lambda exists to further educate individuals about Pan-Asian culture, while keeping our own identities. We aim for academic excellence, keeping in mind the importance of education and learning as the key to strength, awareness and fulfillment.

name: Kappa Sigma
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Kappa Sigma focuses on the Four Pillars of Fellowship, Leadership, Scholarship, and Service.

name: Lambda Chi Alpha
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: We believe in Lambda Chi Alpha Fraternity  and its traditions, principles and ideals. The crescent is our symbol; pure, high ever growing, and the cross is our guide; denoting service, sacrifice, and even suffering and humiliation before the world, bravely endured if need be, in following that ideal. May we have faith in Lambda Chi Alpha and passion for its welfare. May we have hope for the future of Lambda Chi Alpha and strength to fight for its teachings. May we have pure hearts, that we may approach the ideal of perfect brotherly love.

name: Lambda Phi Epsilon
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Lambda Phi Epsilon offers an eternal brotherhood that values trust and loyalty. Founded on February 25, 1981 in UCLA, Lambda Phi Epsilon is the widely renown as the largest and preeminent international Asian interest fraternal organization, providing outstanding leadership, philanthropy, and advocacy in the community. Our mission is to guide each brother on a lifelong discovery of authenticity and personal growth. As we are all grounded by our motto, "To Be Leaders Among Men," we bring together a diverse and dynamic group of men who share interests, concerns, backgrounds and cultures, and who seek to create an impact on our community.

name: Lambda Pi Chi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Latinas Promoviendo Comunidad is the first Latina-focused sorority founded at an Ivy-league institution, we were established on April 16, 1988 at Cornell University.  Patricia Rivera, Maria Caban, Eva Marie Sosa, Migdalia Franklin and Irma Almirall-Padamsee strove to establish an organization that would transcend their collegiate experience and consolidate their strength as responsible leaders of the community.  They worked diligently to develop an impactful organization whose mission and goals would encompass the experiences of all women, but especially those of U.S. Latinas and whose ideals would nurture the growth of its members throughout their lives.

name: Lambda Theta Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO)
description: The mission of Lambda Theta Phi is to empower the Latin male through scholarship, Brotherhood, opportunity, and protection of identity and equality.

name: Omega Phi Beta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO)
description: Our purpose is to Serve and Educate people of diverse backgrounds through sisterhood, leadership, and guidance. As positive role models, we promote unity of all cultures, focus on the empowerment of our gender and raise the standards of excellence in our academic, social, and personal endeavors.

name: Phi Beta Sigma
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity was founded at Howard University in Washington, D.C., January 9, 1914, by three young African-American male students. The Founders, Honorable A. Langston Taylor, Honorable Leonard F. Morse, and Honorable Charles I. Brown, wanted to organize a Greek letter fraternity that would truly exemplify the ideals of brotherhood, scholarship, and service. The Founders deeply wished to create an organization that viewed itself as "a part of" the general community rather than "apart from" the general community. They believed that each potential member should be judged by his own merits, rather than his family background or affluence…without regard to race, nationality, skin tone or texture of hair. They desired for their fraternity to exist as part of an even greater brotherhood which would be devoted to the "inclusive we" rather than the "exclusive we". From its inception, the Founders also conceived Phi Beta Sigma as a mechanism to deliver services to the general community. Rather than gaining skills to be utilized exclusively for themselves and their immediate families, they held a deep conviction that they should return their newly acquired skills to the communities from which they had come. This deep conviction was mirrored in the Fraternity's motto, "Culture For Service and Service For Humanity".

name: Phi Gamma Delta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: We seek to uphold our core values which include Friendship, Knowledge, Service, Morality, and Excellence. Members are encouraged to live by three priorities by these respective order: scholarship, fraternity, and self.

name: Phi Kappa Tau
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek

name: Pi Beta Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: The mission of Pi Beta Phi Fraternity for Women is to promote friendship, develop women of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service. In March of 1918, the Beta Phi Fraternity was founded here at Cornell University. Under the supervision of Miss Louise Case, Beta Phi began working toward its goal of petitioning for a charter of Pi Beta Phi. The future 13 charter members had to submit to the closest investigation as to character, activities, scholarship, and personality. These women were as follows: Helen Miriam Sharrett, Margaret Lounsbury Winfield, Josephine Augusta Sniffen, Mary Alexandria Wheeler, Cornelia Elizabeth Lerch, Evelyn Gertrude Richmond, Elizabeth Dorothy Worman, Grace Brown Blauvelt, Eleanor Margaret Edmonds, Mary Irene Frank and Alice Juliet Street. On June 14, 1919, the Beta Phi Fraternity of Cornell University became a chapter of Pi Beta Phi. These founding sisters of New York Delta meeting Risley Hall, a new dormitory for women at the time. After receiving their charter, they rented a small bungalow on Eddy Street-- the first New York Delta sorority house. From Eddy, Pi Beta Phi moved to Kelvin Place. In 1937, the group leases a house on 425 Wycoff Ave. Finally, in 1955, Pi Phi bought a plot of land on Triphammer Road. While the new house was being built, the sisters lived at 516 University Ave. In 1956, the first sisters moved into what is still our New York Delta House.

name: Pi Delta Psi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: Pi Delta Psi is an Asian-interest cultural Fraternity founded on February 20, 1994 at Binghamton University in Binghamton, New York. Since our founding, the primary mission of Pi Delta Psi has been to spread Asian American Cultural awareness in an effort to empower the entire Asian American community. We are guided by four pillars; Academic Achievement, Cultural Awareness, Righteousness, and Friendship/Loyalty.

name: Pi Kappa Alpha
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: PIKE was recolonized in the Spring of 2013 with about 70 men. Pi Kappa Alpha is dedicated to developing men of integrity, intellect, and high moral character and to fostering a truly lifelong fraternal experience. To fulfill this mission, Pi Kappa Alpha will: Ôû¬ Encourage all our members to live the values taught in our ritual. Ôû¬ Provide innovative services and programs designed to enrich the lives of our undergraduates, alumni, and communities. Ôû¬ Create opportunities for our undergraduate and alumni members to participate in the life of Pi Kappa Alpha on a daily basis. Ôû¬ Promote and foster a spirit of pride, loyalty, inclusion and respect for Pi Kappa Alpha and its rich history. Ôû¬ Empower our undergraduate and alumni members to help shape Pi Kappa Alpha's future by being informed ambassadors and involved advocates. Ôû¬ Encourage our undergraduate and alumni members to take an active role in advancing Pi Kappa Alpha's interests by volunteering their time and by contributing to the fraternity's annual giving campaign. Ôû¬ Communicate effectively and efficiently with our alumni, students and host institutions through various channels on a continuous basis. Ôû¬ Value academic achievement and practice academic integrity. Ôû¬ Establish positive and lasting relationships with our host institutions, alumni and communities. Ôû¬ Encourage our members to be of strong mind and body.

name: Pi Kappa Phi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: For over 100 years Pi Kappa Phi has been building better men on college campuses across the country. From our humble roots at the College of Charleston to over 131 campuses today, Pi Kappa Phi stands for a commitment to fundamental values. We are a first CLASS fraternity which firmly believes in the tenets of Character, Leadership, Academics, Sportsmanship, and Service. These principles are not only valued but instilled through leading-edge educational, service and leadership opportunities. Here at Cornell, The Psi Chapter of Pi Kappa Phi upholds the highest traditions of CLASS, with the drive to lead, to cherish, and to build better men.

name: Sigma Alpha Epsilon
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: To promote and exemplify our core values of scholarship, service, leadership, and friendship.

name: Sigma Alpha Mu
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: To foster and maintain among its sons a spirit of fraternity, a spirit of mutual moral aid and support; to instill and maintain in the hearts of its sons love for and loyalty to Alma Mater and its ideals; to inculcate among its sons such ideals as will result in actions worthy of the highest precepts of true manhood, democracy, and humanity.

name: Sigma Chi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Sigma Chi, the second largest fraternity in the nation, is one of the most influential and highly respected at Cornell. In our 105 years, the Alpha Phi chapter has been characterized by its tight-knit brotherhood and commitment to excellence in academics and athletics. Since 1925, Sigma Chi brothers have made their home in elegant Greystone Manor. The extensive grounds feature beautiful medieval stonework, and a park-like backyard complete with a spacious in-ground swimming pool and small gorge. Sigma Chi brothers actively participate in many influential roles on the hill. The brotherhood boasts both varsity and junior varsity athletes in soccer, baseball, football, basketball, rugby, skiing, squash and water polo. In addition, we have several campus leaders including members of the Interfraternity Council, the ROTC and Student Wishmakers. Our largest philanthropic effort, Derby Days, has traditionally been one of the most lucrative and largely attended charity events on campus. The Alpha Phi chapter of Sigma Chi has long been dedicated to being the premier fraternity at Cornell and our success can only be attributed to the outstanding individuals who make up our brotherhood. Sigma Chi welcomes you to rush and we look forward to seeing you at Greystone.

name: Sigma Delta Tau
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: The mission of Sigma Delta Tau is to enrich the college experience of women of similar ideals, to build lasting friendships and to foster personal growth. Sigma Delta Tau shall encourage each member by providing intellectual, philanthropic, leadership and social opportunities within the framework of mutual respect and high ethical standards

name: Sigma Gamma Rho
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: It is the mission of Sigma Gamma Rho Sorority, Inc. to enhance the quality of life for women and their families in the U.S. and globally through community service, civil, and social action. Our goal is to achieve greater progress in the areas of education, health awareness, and leadership development. Our members, affiliates, staff, and community partners work to create and support initiatives that align with our vision.

name: Sigma Lambda Upsilon
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: In 1993, six women recognized a need for diversity and wanted to create a voice for women on their campus. They sought out an organization that would inspire them with its professionalism, determination, leadership, cultural awareness, academic excellence, and most of all everlasting sisterhood. When they came across Sigma Lambda Upsilon/Se├▒oritas Latinas Unidas Sorority, Inc. they felt and knew that this was the one. The Iota Chapter of Sigma Lambda Upsilon/Se├▒oritas Latinas Unidas Sorority, Inc. has strived to create a unique organization for women that fosters leadership, a dedication to community service, respect, support, student activism and cultural awareness. Even at its most challenging times, the Hermanas of the Iota Chapter have held a strong commitment to these goals and ideals. They have harnessed academic and cultural resources to bring innovative, challenging programming to Cornell's campus. Such programing has covered themes as varied as the Indigenous and African aspects of Latino-Caribbean cultures, career opportunities within public service, the depiction of Hip Hop culture in the media and the role of the visual arts in activism.

name: Sigma Nu
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: To develop ethical leaders inspired by the principles of Love, Honor, and Truth. To foster the personal growth of each man's mind, heart, and character. To perpetuate lifelong friendships and commitment to the Fraternity.

name: Sigma Pi
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: Founded on February 26, 1897 at Vincennes University by William Raper Kennedy, James Thompson Kingsbury, George Martin Patterson, and Rolin Rosco James, it started as Tau Phi Delta (╬ñ╬ª╬ö), a literary society with fraternal ideals. Tau Phi Delta changed its name to The Sigma Pi Fraternity, United States in 1907 and began establishing new chapters that same year. With the establishment of the Fraternity's first Canadian chapter in 1984, the organization's name was changed to The Sigma Pi Fraternity, International. The Fraternity was the first of its kind to be founded west of the Ohio Valley and a charter member of the North-American Interfraternity Conference. Today, Sigma Pi consists of 136 active collegiate groups, dozens of alumni clubs, and over 100,000 initiates. VISION STATEMENT Sigma Pi Fraternity is the leading, international men's collegiate fraternal organization which provides training, guidance and innovative opportunities for: Leadership Development Social and Personal Development Academic Achievement Community Service Heightened Moral Awareness For its brothers throughout their lives.

name: Zeta Beta Tau
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek
description: The Kappa Chapter of Zeta Beta Tau has a rich tradition of excellence at Cornell University. As one of ZBT's oldest and strongest chapters, Kappa Chapter has initiated more than 1,500 men into the Brotherhood since its founding more than 100 years ago. Zeta Beta Tau Fraternity was founded in 1898 in New York City and is now the world's oldest and largest Jewish fraternity. For more than 50 years, Zeta Beta Tau has been a non-sectarian Brotherhood of Equals, and for more than 25 years ZBT has been a pioneer in the fight against hazing, having abolished all two-tier membership statuses and pledging practices in 1989. ZBT is represented on nearly 90 campuses across North America and has initiated more than 130,000 brothers. Over the years Kappa Chapter has figured prominently in the history of ZBT. Several International Presidents of the Fraternity have been alumni of the Kappa Chapter, along with numerous other Cornellians who have served the Fraternity in various significant roles. Historically, the Kappa Chapter of Zeta Beta Tau has resided on one of the most beautiful pieces of land in the Ithaca area, 1 Edgecliff Place on North Campus. The view from the house includes the largest gorge in the region as well as a panorama of downtown Ithaca and Cayuga Lakes.

name: Zeta Phi Beta
category: Sorority & Fraternity Student Organization (SFSO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural
description: To foster the ideas of service, charity, scholarship, civil and cultural endeavors, sisterhood and finer womanhood. These ideals are reflected in the sorority's national program for which its members and auxiliary groups provide voluntary service to staff, community outreach programs, fund scholarships, support organized charities, and promote legislation for social and civic change.

name: Adam Smith Society at Cornell Johnson
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Political/Speech/Debate
description: The Adam Smith Society is a nationwide, chapter-based association of MBA students and business leaders who work to promote on-campus debate and discussion about the moral, social, and economic benefits of capitalism.

name: AFRICAN GRADUATE STUDENTS ASSOCIATION AT CORNELL
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services
description: AfriGA’s mission is to create a welcoming and supportive community for African graduate students at Cornell University. We are committed to promoting academic excellence, celebrating our cultural heritage, and empowering our members to achieve personal and professional success.

name: Amber Dance Troupe
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Performing Arts
description: Amber Dance Troupe's purpose is to spread the rich heritage of Chinese culture and the beauty of Chinese dance to Cornell and local community. Anyone interested can learn Chinese dance skills through regular practice and get opportunity to perform on various stages.

name: American Society of Landscape Architects Cornell Graduate Chapter
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Landscape architects lead the planning, design, and stewardship of healthy, equitable, safe, and resilient environments. The Society’s mission is to advance landscape architecture through advocacy, communication, education, and fellowship. The ASLA at Cornell University exists to support the students of the Department of Landscape Architecture in meeting their academic and professional goals, advocate for the profession of Landscape Architecture on and off campus, and harness the skills of its members to design and work for more accessible, sustainable, and beautiful spaces.

name: Asian Studies Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of the Asian Studies Graduate Student Association shall be to build community among and advocate for graduate students in the fields of Asian Studies and Asian Literature, Religion & Culture.

name: Baker Real Estate Student Organization
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business
description: The Baker Real Estate Student Organization (BSO) aims to serve as a vital bridge between the students and the administration within our business school. Our mission is to amplify the student voice, ensuring that our collective concerns, ideas, and aspirations are heard and addressed by the administration. Additionally, BSO is dedicated to fostering a sense of community and camaraderie among students through various events and activities, providing opportunities for socialization, networking, and personal growth. By promoting active engagement and collaboration, BSO strives to enhance the overall student experience and contribute to a supportive and dynamic academic environment.

name: Biodiversify Affiliates at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Biodiversify Affiliates at Cornell aims to make biology teaching more accurate and inclusive with respect to many axes of diversity, including LGBTQ+ identity, racial identity, disability status, etc.  We work closely with Project Biodiversify (projectbiodiversify.org) but are not officially a part of the Project Biodiversify organization or any non-Cornell organization.

name: Black in Public Policy
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services
description: Black in Public Policy exists to cultivate a supportive community for Black students, faculty, and staff. We aim to foster an environment where Black students feel respected, seen, valued, and heard. Through advocacy, mentorship, and service, we are committed to promoting accessibility, holistic wellness, and a deep sense of fellowship. Our mission is to champion diversity and inclusion through increasing the presence of Black scholars, fostering an environment that retains faculty and staff dedicated to the intersections of race and public policy, and enhancing the academic and cultural experience for all.

name: Cayuga Windsurfing Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: The Cayuga Windsurfing Club was formed by a handful of enthusiasts in an effort to rejuvenate the sport of windsurfing on Cayuga Lake in Tompkins County, NY. With the generous help from Cornell University and The Merrill Sailing Center at East Shore, as well as some equipment donations from various individuals, we intend to create a fun environment for learning windsurfing skills and a community of long lasting friendships for people with a common interests and goals in the sport of windsurfing.

name: Chabad Graduate Students
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: "Chabad Graduate Students" exists to serve the Jewish needs of Cornell Graduate students. We provide learning opportunities, social interactions, speakers, shabbat meals, and holiday celebrations.

name: Chemists for Outreach and Graduate Inclusion
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The purpose of COrGI shall be to build a more inclusive environment within the chemistry department at Cornell by: 1)	Promoting diversity within chemistry 2)	Advocating for departmental policies related to diversity and inclusion 3)	Hosting outreach events targeted towards underrepresented groups 4)	Providing workshops, info-sessions, and an open space where graduate and undergraduate students can have their voices heard and get the support they need to pursue their academic and career goals.

name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: The purpose of the LDSSA shall be to fortify the Cornell LDS community, to raise awareness and education regarding the LDS faith, and to work cooperatively with other faiths in strengthening and building the Cornell community through service, dialog and fun events.

name: COLLIS Institute for Catholic Thought and Culture
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: COLLIS's mission to create and foster a student community in support and partnership with COLLIS Institute, a Catholic institute associated with Cornell University.

name: Colombian Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of the Colombian Association shall be to create a community of solidarity and networking among the Colombian community at Cornell University and any other member of the community interested in the country. It aims to be a collective space to offer collective support, networking, to encourage research and interdisciplinarity.

name: Community Gardens at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: We have 3 purposes. One is to rent for a modest charge that includes plowing, compost, cover crops, and water, garden plots to Cornell students and members of the Cornell family and community. Second, we furnish surplus vegetables we grow to the local food banks .Third, we encourage Cornell scientists and researchers to visit and watch what we do in case we can provide some location that may assist their research.

name: Community Impact Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, AFFILIATION: Johnson School
description: Community Impact serves as a platform for the Johnson community to engage and give back to the local Ithaca community through volunteering, fundraising, and learning from the relationships among the for-profit, non-profit, and public sectors, and promoting socially responsible business.

name: Corean Graduate Catholic Community at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: To provide a ground for Korean or people of Korean descents who believe in Roman Catholicism to carry out and continue the work of Jesus Christ on Earth through fellowships and different activities.

name: Cornell Advancing Science and Policy Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Learn about and create a community interested in science policy issues, educate the public about science and policy, & prepare for a career in science policy, industry, or media.

name: Cornell Catholic Graduate and Professional Student Group
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: The purpose of our organization is to create a community of Catholic graduate and professional students at Cornell and encourage the discussion of topics related to the Catholic faith and life as a professional or graduate student.

name: Cornell Chapter of International City/County Management Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of the Cornell University City/County Management Association shall be to integrate students into the local government management profession by providing a connection to local government leaders, resources, and the ICMA Code of Ethics. Additionally, we serve as a leadership pipeline by developing the next generation of local government professionals through networking opportunities, skill development, mentorship, and professional engagement, including free access to resources and the annual ICMA conference.

name: Cornell Contra Dance Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The purpose of Cornell Contra Dance Club shall be to promote and facilitate engagement in contra dancing in the Cornell community.

name: Cornell Graduate Product Management Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of the Cornell Graduate Product Management Club shall be to empower graduate students to envision, design, and develop impactful products through cross-disciplinary collaboration, bridging academia and industry via experiential learning opportunities, and fostering a community of future leaders equipped with the skills, resources, and networks to drive meaningful innovation

name: Cornell Indoor Futsal Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The purpose of CORNELL INDOOR FUTSAL CLUB shall be to promote community, belonging, and fitness through a shared passion for the sport of futsal.

name: Cornell Law Squash Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, PROF: Law, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: To promote wellness and camaraderie in the Law School community through use of Myron Taylor Hall's athletic facilities.

name: Cornell Negotiation Student Society
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Political/Speech/Debate, AFFILIATION: Brooks School
description: The Cornell Negotiation Student Society commits itself to promoting the interpersonal skills of negotiation, mediation, conflict resolution, and alike pursuits; to promoting scholarship in the aforementioned fields; to encouraging diversity in people and thought in the aforementioned fields.

name: Cornell Turkish Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of Cornell Turkish Graduate Student Association is to unite Turkish graduate students across disciplines, promote Turkish culture and values, support academic excellence and professional development, and serve as a bridge fostering collaboration, dialogue, and cross-cultural exchange between Türkiye and the Cornell community.

name: Cryosphere Community at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The Cryosphere Community at Cornell seeks to unite students, faculty, and staff in a collaborative environment focused on exploring and advancing knowledge of the cryosphere, fostering interdisciplinary research, and strengthening connections within the Cornell community.

name: Design Connect
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: Design Connect provides design and planning services for local municipalities and non-profits that may not have the resources to hire professionals while offering practical experience to students.

name: Development Sociology Graduate Student Collective
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: This organization is designed to help organize and fund activities for graduate students interested in the field of Development Sociology and to support graduate student exposure to the field.

name: Diversity in Cornell Economics
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Student Groups for Student Services
description: To foster diversity in economics at Cornell and in the profession more broadly, and to work toward creating an environment where everyone, particularly individuals from underrepresented groups, feels welcome, respected, and included.

name: ECE Graduate Organization
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: The philosophy of this organization is to provide a welcoming environment for all ECE graduate students, faculty and staff and to further improve the sense of belonging through networking and social events.

name: EMBA Consulting Club at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Executive MBA
description: The EMBA Consulting Club at Cornell is committed to empowering Executive MBA students and alumni by providing strategic insights into the consulting landscape, fostering skill development, and facilitating meaningful networking opportunities. Through workshops, mentorship, and industry engagement, we prepare our members for successful consulting careers while strengthening our community of driven professionals.

name: Evo-Group
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Evo-group is a inter-departmental graduate student run organization that unites undergraduate, graduate students, post-docs, and faculty interested in evolutionary biology. We hold monthly seminars in which students, post-docs, and faculty present their research which they are conducting at Cornell. All Cornell community members are welcome to attend these seminars. We also hold annual meetings in which all evo-group members participate in order to prioritize and plan future directions. We additionally host a one day symposium that highlights a particular topic in evolutionary biology and includes local speakers from nearby Universities in addition to speakers from across Cornell departments.

name: Executive MBA Entrepreneurship Club at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business
description: The purpose of Executive MBA Entrepreneurship Club at Cornell shall be to cultivate entrepreneurial leadership, innovation, and venture creation within the Cornell Executive MBA community. We serve as a platform for EMBA students to explore and accelerate entrepreneurial ideas, connect with like-minded peers, engage with seasoned founders and investors, and gain the skills and resources needed to launch and grow impactful businesses. Our programming aims to host and/or collaborate on events such as hands-on workshops, startup showcases, pitch competitions, industry roundtables, and networking events with alumni, venture capitalists, and thought leaders. By bridging academic insights with real-world applications, the club empowers members to transform ideas into viable ventures while fostering a collaborative, high-trust community that reflects the diverse perspectives and ambitions of Cornell EMBA students. The goals of this organization are to inspire, equip, and connect executive-level leaders in their entrepreneurial journey. Our mission is to: - Inspire: Cultivate an entrepreneurial mindset that embraces innovation, resilience, and calculated risk-taking for both current and aspiring entrepreneurs. - Equip: Provide practical tools to transform ideas into scalable ventures. - Connect: Build a powerful network of students, alumni, faculty, and industry experts to foster collaboration, partnerships, and investment opportunities across the broader entrepreneurial ecosystem within Cornell and beyond. - Encourage: Cultivate entrepreneurial leadership development and knowledge sharing. Through these pillars, we aim to position Cornell EMBA students as catalysts for innovation and economic growth across industries and geographies.

name: Executive Nurse Leadership Network Club at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business
description: The purpose of Executive Nurse Leadership Network Club at Cornell shall be to empower nurses and healthcare leaders to drive strategic innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and ethical governance across clinical and academic settings, increasing awareness of nursing’s diverse impact—from bedside to the boardroom.

name: Expanding Your Horizons at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: The primary purpose of Expanding Your Horizons is to organize a day-long conference in the spring semester which will be open to 7-9th grade girls from all over New York state. The goals of the conference are to stimulate the participants' interest in math and science through hands-on activities, to provide them with female scientist role models (who are Cornell University graduate and undergraduate students), and to foster awareness of opportunities in math and science-related careers. We also provide community for like-minded graduate student interested in science outreach and working on making STEM more inclusive and equitable.

name: Faith and Environment Collective
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Support and strengthen a vibrant community of Christian graduate students, faculty, and staff who, as scholars and professionals, will be prepared to tackle ecological justice and environmental challenges within their fields while living out their Christian faith in their lives and work

name: Free Space Dance
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Performing Arts
description: Free Space Dance Club is a vibrant, inclusive community of over 300 graduate and undergraduate students at Cornell University who share a passion for dance. We provide workshops in hip hop, jazz, and K-pop that welcome dancers of all levels — from complete beginners to experienced performers. Our mission is to create a supportive environment where members can explore movement, improve their skills, stay active, and connect with others through the joy of dance.

name: GEEKS - Grads Employing Empathy, Knowledge, & Service
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: The reasons that this organization was formed include the following: A. To allow CU graduate students the opportunity to serve the community B. To provide an avenue by which CU graduate students can travel the world to help others in need C. To assist CU graduate students in advancing scientific outreach within the Ithaca area as well as areas affected by the group's service projects D. To cultivate a sensitivity among CU graduate students to the circumstances of communities in need E. To promote and encourage leadership among CU graduate students

name: Geothermal Rising Student Chapter at Cornell University
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Engage the broader student community in leveraging the power provided by the Earth through various professional development opportunities to facilitate and promote the understanding of geothermal energy, its practical applications and its role in the global transition to renewable energy usage.

name: Grad Student Improv Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Performing Arts
description: The club's mission is to provide a space for graduate students to perform improvisational theater.  We want to support graduate students in balancing academic and personal lives by providing a space where they can relax their minds and expand and reevaluate their mindset towards life's circumstances. This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

name: Graduate Association of Chemistry
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Student Groups for Student Services
description: To organize social, professional, and outreach events and opportunities for graduate students to network.

name: Graduate Christian Fellowship at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: GCF exists to foster spiritual formation, witness and service, the integration of faith and learning, and Christian community through a variety of activities including: Bible studies, large group worship time, annual retreats, roundtable discussions, and community service projects.

name: Graduate Student Veterans Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The Graduate Student Military Community serves as a unifying body for Cornell University's graduate students who have military experience or connections - including those who have served, their families, and their supporters. Our mission is to foster a sense of belonging and community grounded in shared experience and mutual support. Our organization is dedicated to advancing the academic, professional, and social well-being of our members, and we work to ensure they thrive throughout their graduate experience.

name: Healthcare Artificial Intelligence Collaborative Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business, AFFILIATION: Executive MBA
description: The purpose of HAI-C is to nurture a community of students and professionals from diverse backgrounds interested in AI/ML . This club will serve as a platform for exchanging ideas and promoting ethical adoption, thereby advancing the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare. It ensures that members remain at the forefront of AI and machine learning innovations within the industry.

name: Hotel Graduate Student Organization
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: Our mission is to serve and benefit students in the Master of Management in Hospitality at Cornell University, and the entire graduate and professional student body at Cornell University.

name: India Association at Cornell University
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: We aim to foster an environment of comfort and camaraderie among International students in Cornell's Graduate and Professional schools, with a focus on students of Indian origin. Also, we strive to spread awareness and celebrate Indian culture in all its vivid glory.

name: Iranian Graduate Students
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of IGS shall be to serve as a substrate for social, academic, and cultural interactions between current and prospective Iranian graduate students, and the Cornell community at large.

name: JD-MBA Society
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Law
description: The purpose of the Society shall be to promote Cornell's JD-MBA Program, foster communication among its members, plan social gatherings, and strengthen ties between JD-MBA students and alumni.

name: Jewish Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: The purpose of the Jewish Graduate Student Association shall be to provide Jewish Cornell graduate and professional students in all programs and degree paths (and their friends and partners) and Jewish young professionals in the Ithaca area with community, social events, and a network for support and resources.

name: Johnson Cornell F1 Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Student Groups for Student Services
description: Our mission is to to be a place where students who like Formula 1 can meet and talk about Formula 1 races along the year.

name: Johnson Crew
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: At Johnson Crew, our mission is to foster a vibrant community of MBA students united by a passion for rowing.

name: Johnson FC
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: To provide a community for Cornell graduate school students to play, watch, and follow soccer together.

name: Johnson Gaming Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Gaming/Esports
description: The Johnson Gaming Club brings classmates together through video games and board games, creating a space to have fun, meet people, and build community! The club also offers an opportunity to learn more about the video game industry and connect with others who share an interest in gaming.

name: Johnson Golf Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The Johnson - Golf Club's mission is to promote the game of golf in the Johnson community through friendly competition and member education. The Johnson Golf Club was created to facilitate student learning and mastery of the game of golf. In addition, golf will be used as a networking tool to promote interaction among students, faculty, alumni, and recruiters.

name: Johnson Ice Hockey Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: Play hockey and have fun

name: Johnson on Tap
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Food/Drink, AFFILIATION: Johnson School
description: Johnson on Tap brings the Cornell Johnson community together through a shared appreciation of beer. Our mission is to create welcoming, social experiences that strengthen bonds among students, alumni, and partners, while fostering curiosity about traditions and cultures around the world.

name: Johnson Outdoor Ventures Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: The Outdoor Ventures Club provides an opportunity for the Johnson community to take advantage of the numerous outdoor activities in Ithaca and the surrounding areas.

name: Johnson Poker Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Gaming/Esports, Tabletop Games
description: The purpose of Johnson Poker Club is to provide a platform for poker enthusiasts to come together for poker nights, and to provide an opportunity to learn poker, foster camaraderie within the Johnson community and participate in poker tournaments.

name: Johnson Ski & Snowboard Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: The Ski Club provides that much needed escape from the rigors of business school and fosters a strong community of skiiers and boarders.

name: Johnson Tennis Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: To provide a platform for students of the Johnson Graduate School of Management and other graduate students on campus to engage in recreational tennis.

name: Johnson Wine and Spirits Club
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Food/Drink, AFFILIATION: Johnson School
description: Johnson Wine & Spirits is designed to promote wine and spirit education and appreciation through lectures, tastings, speakers and various other events.

name: Korean Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of KGSA is to perform the following functions: (1) To enhance the relationships among Korean graduate students. (2) To promote relationships with other communities, both here at Cornell University and internationally. (3) To provide a means for Korean graduate students at Cornell University to obtain pertinent information related to career development and establish a social network to benefit them after graduation. (4) To serve as a liaison between the administration, the Korean graduate students at Cornell and other organizations. (5) To provide social, cultural and educational functions for Korean graduate students as well as the general student body at Cornell.

name: L.H. Bailey’s Botany Bunch – Botanical Society of America Cornell Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife
description: The Mission of L.H. Bailey’s Botany Bunch – Botanical Society of America Cornell Student Chapter shall be to fulfill responsibilities of a Botanical Society of America student chapter, to promote interest in botanical subjects, provide botanical themed events, and serve as a resource for students about Botanical Society of America grants, programs, and other opportunities. This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.

name: Latine Graduate Student Coalition
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of the Latine Graduate Student Coalition is to provide a forum for graduate and professional students to support one another in achieving academic excellence and recognition. While centering the experiences, needs, and voices of Latine students, LGSC welcomes all graduate and professional students committed to its mission.

name: LAW - American Constitution Society the Cornell Law School Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: The American Constitution Society for Law and Policy is a progressive legal organization that promotes the U.S. Constitutional values of "individual rights and liberties, genuine equality, access to justice, democracy and the rule of law."

name: LAW - Asian Pacific American Law Student Association
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Law, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: This organization shall adhere to the philosophy that diversity will always enlarge our understanding of the different values that need to be understood as we enter the global economy; that unity should be embraced so that we may assist the less fortunate members of our Asian community; and that leadership will take on many forms, and ultimately is a very individualistic decision based on no arbitrary set definition.

name: LAW - Basketball Group
category: Grad/Professional General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, AFFILIATION: Law School
