description: JLPP's mission is to edit and publish scholarly articles and notes in the fields of law and public policy.

name: LAW - Legal Information Institute Supreme Court Bulletin
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Publication/Media, PROF: Law, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: The LII Supreme Court Bulletin is a student-run publication associated with Cornell's Legal Information Institute.  LII Supreme Court Bulletin provides student-written previews of every upcoming United States Supreme Court case to over 14,000 e-mail subscribers and millions of visitors to the LII website.  While many of these readers are lawyers and judges, many are reporters, police officers, and other educated non-lawyers.  The previews contain far more than a mere recitation of the facts and the procedural posture below.  Each case preview provides a thoughtful and neutral analysis of the legal arguments on either side and identifies the underlying issues that make each case important to the public.  Our readers get a sense of not just what the Supreme Court is doing, but also why.

name: LAW - LLM Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Law, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: The purpose of the LLM Association is to represent the LLM student body at Cornell University Law School.  The LLMA holds scholarly and social student events.

name: LAW - Older Wiser Law Students (O.W.L.S.) at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: The purpose of Older Wiser Law Students (OWLS) shall be to foster a supportive community for students who have taken significant time off prior to law school; are transitioning into second careers; are partnered, married, and/or parenting; or view their academic path as non-traditional. We define a significant amount of time as 5 years or more separated from an undergraduate institution. The group caters to the social, academic, and other needs of those who are transitioning back to student life after a number of years out of school or who have serious non-academic commitments that fall outside of class.

name: LAW - Public Interest Law Union
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Law, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: Law School
description: Cornell Law School's Public Interest Law Union offers opportunities for students interested in a public interest legal career to explore the diversity of career options available to them. The group hosts public interest speaker events, provides volunteer service opportunities for members of the law school, and helps raise funds for grants for law students working in a Public Interest job in the summer.

name: Linguistics Circle at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: The CLC serves to promote exchange of ideas among graduate students in the field and to advocate for the graduate student body within the department. Throughout the course of the academic year the CLC invites a series of outside speakers from linguistics departments around the country and the world. Speakers deliver talks attended by faculty, graduate and undergraduate students (followed by a reception) and are often available for one-on-one meetings with interested graduate students. The CLC also publishes The Proceedings of SALT, which contains articles developed from work presented at the annual Semantics and Linguistic Theory conference. We also organize workshops and social events, and we curate an array of resources for linguistics graduate students, such as a library, a database of teaching materials, and a variety of useful links and information.

name: MAC Doctoral Peer Mentoring Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: The MAC Mentoring Program is a graduate student-run initiative from the Graduate School Office of Inclusion & Student Engagement (OISE). Designed to address the needs of a diversity of doctoral students across all graduate fields through peer mentoring, this program focuses on helping new graduate students identify and form community at Cornell. MAC strives to promote a social environment that is inclusive of all doctoral students at Cornell. During the academic year, MAC hosts two monthly events, general body meetings (GBMs) and MAC-Meetups, to help broaden and strengthen a sense of community on campus.

name: Materials Science and Engineering Graduate Student Association at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of LATTICE shall be to foster the growth of graduate students by promoting interaction, collaboration, and professional development. Through community-building, education, and advocacy, we aim to cultivate a culture of integrity, excellence, and mutual support that ensures the success of our members and the advancement of materials science research.

name: Media Entertainment & Sports Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Publication/Media, AFFILIATION: Johnson School, Visual Arts
description: To foster community among Johnson Graduate School of Management students interested in professional careers in the media & entertainment industries.

name: Molecular Biology and Genetics Diversity Council
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: The MBG+ Diversity Council is committed to empowering the trainees in the fields of BMCB, GGD, Biophysics, and BBS to foster a culture of inclusion and equity by supporting and providing voices and resources to all those seeking to advance the educational and professional experiences of trainees from historically marginalized groups.  This goal shall be accomplished through such diverse elements as advocacy, peer mentorship, community building events, resources for graduate school success, and supportive statements.

name: MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business
description: The MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell Johnson College of Business is an organization founded in 2022 by students of the M.S. Business Analytics program at SC Johnson Graduate School of Management. The mission of the MSBA Data Science Club at Cornell is to inspire and prepare students to excel in data science and machine learning, providing them with education, skills, and networking opportunities to solve complex business problems through data-driven solutions. We equip our members for DS/ML interviews, facilitate networking with faculty, alumni, and industry professionals, encourage the development of comprehensive data science portfolios, foster participation in competitions and projects, strengthen relationships with academia and industry, and cultivate a diverse and inclusive community. Through these initiatives, the DSC empowers its members to become future leaders, driving innovation and making a positive impact in the business world.

name: Music Graduate Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The Music Graduate Association is the official organization for the graduate students in the Music department. We organize small and large events to help our academic and professional development, and social outings to help foster a sense of community amongst the grad students. We also serve an advocacy role through discussing issues that affect our members at meetings and bringing them to the faculty in our department or GPSA.

name: Neurobiology and Behavior Graduate Student Society
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The purpose of the NBBGSS is to facilitate communication between the graduate students and the faculty in the field of NBB at Cornell. Our goals include disseminating important information to graduate students and acting as a formal voice for graduate students within the workings of the department. Additionally, the NBBGSS fosters community among graduate students in the field by organizing social events and discussion forums.

name: Nutrition Graduate Student Organization
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: NGSO is a graduate student organization at Cornell University established to promote interaction among graduate students in the Division of Nutritional Sciences (DNS) and to facilitate communication and interaction between the graduate students and the DNS faculty and administration.

name: Old Ezra Finance Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Business and Management
description: The Old Ezra Finance Club is committed to enhancing Johnson's presence in the finance industry, while providing its members with educational, recruiting and career development opportunities within Investment Banking, Corporate Finance and Capital Markets. The mission of the club is to prepare members to succeed in recruiting for finance positions across a variety of industries.

name: Organization of Cornell Planners
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Education/Human Services, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The Organization of Cornell Planners (OCP) manages departmental professional development and social events for Master's students of Regional Planning, Historic Preservation Planning, and Regional Science. OCP interfaces with several student groups committed to advancing the field of planning: Design Connect, the Women's Planning Forum, and the International Planning Students Organization are among many student organizations whose activities are promoted and co-sponsored by the OCP. OCP can co-host events with student organizations outside CRP and AAP. OCP also provides mentorships to incoming graduate students with a student mentor-mentee system. Lastly, OCP collects and disseminates information regarding departmental information events, job opportunities in the planning profession, and mixer events to all alumni, faculty, and students affiliated within the Cornell Department of City and Regional Planning.

name: Pandaemonium Germanicum
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services
description: 1.	To foster the social and intellectual environment of graduate students in the Department of German Studies. 2.	To represent the interests and concerns of graduate students in the Department of German Studies. 3.	To participate in the social and intellectual life of the university. 4.	To promote a critical understanding of German Studies. 5.	To address and support the professional development of future academics in the discipline of German Studies.

name: Ph2
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The purpose of our organization is to bring together graduate Linguistics students interested in Phonetics and Phonology. During our meetings, we read articles, practice conference talks, learn new academic skills, and more. We will also organize academic events where we invite guest speakers to give talks and hold meetings with students, as well as social events where students can get to know their peers and faculty better.

name: Physics Graduate Society
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: To foster social wellbeing in the physics graduate community.

name: Plant Biology Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: Coagulation. Community to inspire. Meeting of the minds.

name: Plant Pathology Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: This organization exists to represent and promote the professional activities of graduate students and to facilitate communication among graduate students and between graduate students and faculty of the Field of Plant Pathology and Plant-Microbe Biology at Cornell University. The PPGSA also serves as a grievance board for the students and is actively involved in improving the conditions for graduate study in the department.

name: QGrads
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: QGrads strives: (a) To build a strong community at Cornell by creating spaces for graduate students of all sexual orientations and gender identities to feel heard, seen, and supported. (b) To plan events and programming that promote the personal and professional development of graduate students of all sexual orientations and gender identities. (c) To actively address the needs of our members. (d) To advocate for social justice on and off campus.

name: Retail & Luxury Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Business and Management
description: The Retail & Luxury Club is dedicated to serve Johnson School students interested in seeking a career path in the luxury sector as well as to provide students with an opportunity to understand and network with professionals within these industries.

name: Romance Studies Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Romance Studies Graduate Student Association is an organization for graduate students of all levels and statuses within Cornell's department. While Romance Studies houses the sub-departments of Spanish, French, and Italian, the RSGSA will provide leadership and assembly possibilities that seek to enhance unity and shared interests of all language sections in the department. The student association will work closely with the steering committee to develop programming that helps graduates in their academic and professional efforts. The RSGSA also wishes to support the existing efforts of the French Studies program, the Program in European Studies, as well as existing student groups linked to the Romance Studies department, through better organization. We hope the Romance Studies Graduate Student Association will give the department's graduate students the best opportunity to contribute and share scholarly and professional goals.

name: SAGES - Student Association of the Geneva Experiment Station
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Food/Drink
description: The Student Association of the Geneva Experiment Station (SAGES) is led by students pursing Master's and Doctorate degrees in the agricultural sciences and holds events open to the entire Cornell AgriTech at The New York State Agriculture Experiment Station Community. SAGES exists to promote leadership, to encourage the study of agricultural issues relevant to the State of New York, and to promote a better relationship between the Station and the population of the city of Geneva and surrounding communities. Members have an expressed interest in the advancement of the agricultural sciences through research, outreach, extension, and education. SAGES events include presentations on various research topics, day trips to area attractions, potlucks, fundraising, an annual symposium, among other events. In addition, each year SAGES makes and sells apple cider and then uses the proceeds to fund two $750 scholarships which is awarded to an area high school senior who intends to pursue a career in agriculture.

name: Science & Technology Studies Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Education/Human Services, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of the organization is to work on behalf of the graduate students in the Department of Science and Technology Studies at Cornell. We organize beginning of the year and end of the year events to introduce graduate students to each other and to build our community. We also bring in outside speakers and organize lunch and workshops with them. More recently, we have funded a writers' group which helps students in our department (and those from other departments who would like to join in) work on their writing projects through workshopping either dissertation chapters, journal articles, and conference papers. Since covid, we have organized digital get-togethers, and we helped fund a zoom talk on antiracism in our field, coordinated by current graduate students.

name: Science and Technology Entry Program-Upward Partnership (STEP-UP)
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: STEP-UP strives to increase the exposure of underrepresented, marginalized and low income family high school students to scientific education (graduate and undergraduate). STEP-UP mission  is to positively impact the high school student population in the Ithaca Area through outcome-based programming, scientific exposure, diversity initiatives and interactions with College and Graduate students. Additionally, we want  to foster a community where we can discuss science related current events and increase the understanding of current scientific research.

name: SiGMA: Sibley Graduates in Mechanical & Aerospace
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, Student Groups for Student Services
description: SiGMA is made up of the Graduate students in the Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. This group fosters a strong community among the graduate students by facilitating social, academic, and outreach events.

name: Sloan Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Brooks School
description: The Sloan Student Association facilitates networking opportunities with prospective employers, professional development programs, community service involvement, and formal and informal social activities. Our activities center around the goals of furthering our “Sloan Family” and addressing MHA students’ needs.

name: Snee Graduate Organization
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The mission of the Snee Graduate Organization is to enhance the professional and social interaction between graduate students in the fields of Geological and Atmospheric Sciences. The organization also serves as a medium for communication between the graduate student body and the faculty of the Earth and Atmospheric Sciences at Cornell University.

name: Society for Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: SACNAS strives to promote diversity at Cornell by aiding the success of Chicano/Latino, Native American, and underrepresented students to pursue graduate education and obtain the advanced degrees. SACNAS's mission is to impact the student population through outcome-based programming and diversity initiatives that are necessary for advanced careers in science, research, and leadership positions in STEM.

name: Society of Horticulture Graduate Student Group
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: To provide a unified network of graduate students in the field of horticulture in order to support one another throughout our professional careers. In addition, we strive to promote greater appreciation and knowledge of horticulture in our community.

name: Sociology Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The Cornell Sociology Graduate Student Association (SGSA) began in 2003 to address the needs of Cornell sociology graduate students at each stage of the graduate program. The GSA has continued to be a vital part of the sociology graduate program at Cornell through the organization's active role in enhancing the educational, professional, and social interactions among our graduate students and faculty.

name: Soil and Crop Sciences Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: The goals of this organization are to promote a sense of community and professional development for graduate students and post docs within the Soil and Crop Sciences section.

name: South Asian Business Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AFFILIATION: Johnson School
description: Joining the South Asian Business Club allows students with an interest in the region to network with prominent South Asians in the United States and abroad, express themselves through cultural events, as well as feel at home in Ithaca when families and friends are thousands of miles away. With an increasing number of students who can trace their roots to the region, this club was started to serve as a platform for representing the interests of the students; with career services, alumni, and other student clubs. South Asia includes the following countries: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Maldives. The club comprises of 75+ members within the Johnson School Community.

name: South East Asia Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: To bring together graduate students interested in and/or doing research with aerial concentration in South East Asia.

name: Statistics Graduate Society at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of the SGS is to make all aspects of graduate student life in the field of Statistics -- academic, social, and professional -- more enjoyable, and is responsible for representing graduate students' concerns to The Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Graduate School, and The Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science.

name: Sustainable Global Enterprise Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Business and Management, Sustainability/Environmental
description: To empower future leaders to integrate social and environmental sustainability into business and to advance the professional development of Johnson students interested in sustainability-related careers by providing the Johnson community with forums for networking and education.

name: Synapsis
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Synapsis promotes professional and social interaction among members of the Cornell community interested in plant breeding. In addition, we provide events and educational seminars in order to highlight current research and discoveries in the field.

name: Tropical Biology & Conservation - Graduate Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Understanding and conserving tropical species, ecosystems, landscapes and biodiversity is a major challenge facing society today. Furthermore, anthropogenic effects on the tropics and the human factors (social, cultural, political, and economic) driving such effects, add enormous complexity to such an urgent task. In all, tropical biology and conservation involves complex and coupled ecological and social systems. Therefore, in affiliation with the Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation, Cornell's Tropical Biology and Conservation – Graduate Student Association (TBC-GSA) brings together graduate students and early career scientists across campus to share their research and efforts, while promoting the links between ecological and social dimensions for conserving tropical biodiversity. Interests of TBC-GSA cover a wide array of basic and applied research topics on tropical biology and conservation, including: structure, dynamics and functioning of tropical ecosystems, anthropogenic effects on tropical biodiversity and ecosystems, social-cultural and political-economic drivers of such effects, and more.

name: VC@Johnson
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Business and Management
description: VC@Johnson is the gateway to the venture capital world at Cornell's SC Johnson Graduate School of Management. Our goal is simple: to build a community where Johnson students and industry professionals can connect, learn, and innovate in the venture capital sector. We plan to be the go-to hub for venture capital insights and networking at Johnson.

name: VET - American Association of Bovine Practitioners
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Cornell Student Chapter of the American Association of Bovine Practitioners is an academic organization of future veterinarians. Through our sponsored activities (guest lectures, farm visits, wet labs), we strive to fulfill the mission of the National AABP, an international association of veterinarians serving society as leaders in cattle health, welfare and productivity.

name: VET - American Association of Equine Practitioners Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of SCAAEP is to enable veterinary students at Cornell to learn veterinary medicine as it pertains to equine medicine, both commercial and private, to provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in the equine aspects of veterinary medicine, to aid in the career development of students by informing them of the opportunities available in equine medicine, to enhance leadership characteristics and skills and to act as a liaison between equine veterinarians and students.

name: VET - American Association of Small Ruminant Practitioners - Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: For those who don't have much experience with large animals, AASRP is a great way to ease into the farm animal world! AASRP is a club devoted to teaching students of all interests about the care of goats, sheep, llamas, and alpacas. Activities include various lectures on sheep/goat management, hoof trimming, sheep shearing, wetlabs, venipuncture labs, and visits to local sheep, goat and llama farms. They welcome anyone interested in learning more and interacting more with small ruminants which are rapidly becoming more popular as dairy animals and as pets.

name: VET - American Society of Laboratory Animal Medicine, Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of the Student Chapter of the American Society of Laboratory Animal Practitioners is to foster educational activities in the veterinary specialty of Laboratory Animal Medicine and to familiarize the members with standards, regulations, and techniques pertaining to this discipline.

name: Vet - American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to: 1) To promote the importance of animal behavior in veterinary medicine. 2) To provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in relation to animal behavior, by encouraging guest speakers for Chapter Meetings. 3) To create and maintain an affiliation between Student Chapter members and members of the American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior (AVSAB). 4) To enhance leadership characteristics in its members through organization as a Student Chapter. 5) To encourage camaraderie among veterinary students with an interest in animal behavior. 6) To act as a communication link between practicing animal behaviorists and veterinary students via the AVSAB newsletter. 7) To assist students in participating in externships with practicing veterinarians with a professional interest in Behavior. Students and practitioners are advised to communicate via the AVSAB newsletter, Members only Forum, and through the AVSAB community platform. 8) To allow mention of SCAVSAB membership on curriculum vitae to demonstrate interest in behavior to prospective veterinary employers.

name: VET - Association for Non-traditional Students at Cornell College of Veterinary Medicine
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Community Service, Health/Wellbeing, PROF: Science/Healthcare, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Background and Mission: Despite their increasing presence in the collegiate environment, non-traditional students (NTS) are often overlooked and misunderstood, especially at the graduate level, with universities primarily catering to the needs of traditional students and lacking NTS support services. The definition of an NTS may vary, but a generally agreed upon definition for a non-traditional graduate student is someone who may be older (e.g., 25 years or older) than their fellow students and/or took a detour, rather than a direct route, from undergraduate to graduate school. This definition is inclusive of students who: •	Had a previous career/job before going back to school •	Are parents and/or have dependents •	Are caretakers •	Are military service members/veterans •	Employed full-time and/or goes to school part-time •	And/or financially independent As we march towards a more inclusive environment within veterinary medicine, it is vital to support non-traditional DVM, MPH, and PhD students. Thus, the Association for Non-traditional Students (ANTS) aims to create a sustainable support network for non-traditional DVM, MPH, and PhD students at the Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM). ANTS’ values and vision revolve around the following: •	Building community at Cornell, Ithaca, and beyond (including other DVM, MPH, and STEM PhD programs) •	Being a resource and sharing resources (e.g., student-parent childcare grants, mutual aid, and emergency funds) •	Outreaching to allied groups, programs, NT CVM alumni, and offices to further foster and advocate for the professional and social support of non-traditional students. •	Collaborating with allied groups that support the intersecting identities of NTS (e.g., but not limited to, FGLI, sNABV, PrideSVMC, WVLDI, GSVA, etc.) and also collaborating with multidisciplinary groups to support the diverse career pathways and trajectories of NTS at CVM.

name: VET - Association of Avian Veterinarians Cornell University
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: SCAAV works to enhance the educational opportunities of the veterinary students in the NYSCVM in regard to avian welfare and healthcare, specifically by informing students about veterinary problems and diseases, husbandry issues, preventative medicine, and scientific research currently encountered in dealing with both captive and wild birds.

name: VET - Association of Reptilian and Amphibian Veterinarians ZAWS
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: We aim to train veterinary students so that they can contribute to advancing reptilian and amphibian medicine, surgery, and conservation.  We enhance the educational opportunities of the professional students in the veterinary college to learn about reptilian and amphibian medicine by hosting lectures and wet labs about veterinary problems and diseases, preventative medicine, husbandry issues, and scientific research currently encountered in dealing with both captive and wild exotic species.

name: VET - Association of Veterinary Scientists
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: To enhance collaboration and scientific growth between veterinary students, residents, and researchers interested or involved in veterinary science research.

name: VET - Cardiology Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Cardiology Club organizes cardiology rounds, lectures, and wet labs for veterinary students and other interested members of the veterinary community to support further learning and exposure in the field of cardiology.

name: VET - Cornell Society for Veterinary Pain Management
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: As a student chapter of the International Veterinary Academy of Pain Management, we hope to familiarize students with the multi-faceted world of pain management, as it will be an integral part of their careers and lives.

name: VET - CVM Peer Mentors
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of CVM Peer Mentors shall be to foster an environment that supports the first-year veterinary student’s transition into veterinary school by hosting various events throughout the school year to engage first-year students and the broader CVM community and offer opportunities for camaraderie, enjoyment, and an outlet for academic and personal challenges. As upper-class vet students who advise first-year students, PMs additionally collaborate with faculty and staff to tailor resources to student needs.

name: VET - Dance Collective
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Performing Arts, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of the CUCVM Dance Collective is to bring together the dance community within the Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine by celebrating our enthusiasm for art, music, and dance.  As a non-audition based dance group open to students of any level and style of dance, we serve as a creative outlet for students who would like a fun and casual way to express movement and meet others with similar interests during our bi-monthly open classes.  In addition to this, the CUCVM Dance Collective also offers performance opportunities to those students who would like the chance to choreograph and perform.  Such opportunities include our annual Spring Showcase, which provides student choreographers a venue where they can present their work to the entire community.

name: VET - Dermatology Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Dermatological issues are one of the most common reasons companion animals are brought to the vet office. They are hard to deal with, incredibly uncomfortable, and truly take a toll on our pets' quality of life. The goal of the Dermatology club is to help future veterinarians feel more comfortable diagnosing and treating skin cases. Through labs, lectures, and shadowing opportunities, students will feel more confident in their PE findings, formulating diagnostic steps, and gain more knowledge about the wonderful world of derm!

name: VET - First Generation Low Income Veterinary Student Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The First Generation, Low Income Veterinary Student Association is dedicated to empowering veterinary students navigating unique challenges by cultivating an inclusive community that fosters academic excellence, leadership, and professional growth. Through mentorship, advocacy, and resource access, we strive to dismantle barriers and provide members with the tools, connections, and support needed to succeed in veterinary medicine. By championing equity, financial literacy, and collaboration, FiGLI advances systemic change to create a more diverse and just veterinary profession where all students can thrive and lead.

name: VET - Jewish Association of Veterinary Students at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Spiritual/Religious
description: The purpose of Jewish Association of Veterinary Students  shall be to provide a safe and inclusive association through which to practice and promote Jewish culture and customs through various events and gatherings, holiday celebrations, and community engagement. The organization also aims to engage with veterinary students interested in learning more about and engaging with Jewish culture and customs to further foster understanding and inclusivity on the veterinary college campus.

name: VET - Latinx Veterinary Medical Association at Cornell Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: To empower Latinx students and professionals in veterinary medicine and support aspiring Latinx veterinarians in order to better serve client demographics or "the next generation of Latinx veterinarians".

name: VET - Pet Loss Support Hotline
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The first Pet Loss Support Hotline was set up in 1989 at the College of Veterinary Medicine at the University of California at Davis. Cornell used their guidelines in construction of our own hotline. The hotline is staffed by volunteer veterinary students who have undergone extensive training with professional grief counselors. Volunteers regularly attend discussion meetings with faculty advisors. These meetings assist hotline volunteers in dealing with the personal responses to grief and educate them to better serve the needs of callers. Literature relating to pet loss and grief is maintained by the hotline and available for mailing to callers who request information. Articles about the human-animal bond and grief are provided for the education of student volunteers and, together with the experience from the hotline, help to prepare the students for the emotional side of veterinary practice. Many if not all of the veterinary student volunteers have experienced the loss of a beloved companion animal and are aware of the profound sadness and confusing emotions that can result. They understand that every loss is unique and they are trained to acknowledge the normal grieving process that callers are experiencing. The Cornell Pet Loss Support Hotline is not a mental health hotline. If the concerns voiced over a call are beyond topics related to pet loss and pet grieving, volunteers will help you find appropriate resources for your needs.

name: VET - Pride Student VMC Cornell (Broad Spectrum)
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Student Pride VMC (formerly Broad Spectrum) strives to support, represent, and advance the interests of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and nonbinary, questioning, intersex, asexual, and otherwise gender/sexuality-marginalized (LGBTQIA+) students, faculty, and staff affiliated with Cornell College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM). We aim to foster inclusivity for LGBTQIA+ persons within the CVM community by organizing safe-space social gatherings, hosting speakers and educational events, advocating for LGBTQIA+ needs within the context of CVM, and collaborating with Pride VMC and other Student Pride VMC chapters to discuss the broader status of LGBTQIA+ individuals in veterinary medicine.

name: VET - Psychopaths: American College of Veterinary Pathologists
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: As a student chapter of the American College of Veterinary Pathology, the Pathology club, aim: To encourage veterinary student involvement in the field of veterinary pathology and provide an additional opportunity for its associates to gain professional knowledge in this field. To make available to the students the opportunities offered by the American College of Veterinary Pathologists to its Student Chapters.

name: VET - Service Dog Training and Education Program at Cornell's College of Veterinary Medicine
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The mission of STEP@Cornell is to promote the presence of assistance animal organizations on campus and assist these organizations by fundraising for them, acting as a liaison between the organizations and the greater Cornell community, educating the vet community about assistance dogs and this unique sector of animal behavior, and providing opportunities to raise and train an assistance dog. STEP@Cornell is dedicated to helping serve the organizations within the community that provide assistance animals to those who need them.

name: VET - Shelter Medicine Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Shelter Medicine Club's mission is to expose veterinary students to the myriad of issues surrounding animal sheltering and animal welfare issues. We collaborate with local shelters to host monthly clinics where students can gain hands-on experience through assisting with surgery prep and post-op care, administering vaccines, and performing physical exams. We host speakers on a wide range of subjects, such as careers in animal sheltering medicine, humane animal handling, rescuing animals during disasters, animal behavior, and pet overpopulation. We often work together with other clubs on animal welfare-related topics, and also host brown bag discussions on various issues.

name: VET - Small Animal Clinical Skills Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Small Animal Clinical Skills Clubs (SACS) at Cornell is devoted to providing students with opportunities to practice and improve their clinical skills. We host lectures and hands-on wet labs taught by residents or hospital technicians that allow students to practice clinical skills on both live animals and practice cadavers. Previous club events have included labs on dental radiography and dental techniques such as scaling and nerve blocks. Two of our most memorable club events include the annual vaccination and SNAP test clinics hosted in the fall and spring. These clinics are open to students, staff, and faculty of the vet school and usually draw in around 60 animals per clinic. The clinics are run entirely by club members and volunteers, and offer students opportunities to perform numerous vaccinations and blood draws under the supervision of our trusted advisers, Pati Kirch (LVT/Teaching Support Specialist), Carolyn McDaniel (VMD/Senior Lecturer, Department of Clinical Sciences), and Patrick Carney (Ph. D, DVM, ACVIM, Associate Professor, Section of Community Practice Service)

name: VET - Society for Veterinary Ophthalmology
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The mission of the Society for Veterinary Ophthalmology is to promote student participation and interest in veterinary ophthalmology by providing opportunities for students to further their education in the field.

name: VET - Southside Healthy Pet Clinic
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The mission of Southside Healthy Pet Clinic shall be to improve animal welfare in Tompkins County and the surrounding area by providing affordable, high-quality veterinary care for low-income residents while enriching the relationship between the Cornell and Ithaca communities.

name: VET - Spay Day
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Spay Day is a veterinary school organization that aims to increase awareness of the need for as well as access to spay/neuter to save animal lives. We aim to give further hands-on experience opportunities to veterinary students. By holding spay/neuter clinics for the community, Spay Day aims to help with animal overpopulation, reduce animal diseases, increase owner education, and teach students the appropriate way to safely and efficiently spay or neuter an animal.

name: VET - Sports Medicine Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: To provide education and information in various aspects of prevention, recognition, care and rehabilitation of injuries within equine and canine sports medicine and to promote the human-animal bond through activities that get people outside and working with their dogs.  These activities may include agility, hiking, herding, tracking, Canine Good Citizen training and testing, and others as chosen by members. All breeds, mutts, sizes, ages, and fitness levels are welcome! Activities will be scheduled to provide students with a variety of dog-friendly options for relaxation and exercise. Lectures will focus on canine and equine athlete maintenance, training, and injuries. The Sports Medicine club believes in Equal Education & Employment https://hr.cornell.edu/about/workplace-rights/equal-education-and-employment Equal Education and Employment | Working at Cornell *Dogs may not be actively aggressive to dogs or people; they do not need to be social butterflies, but cannot constitute a hazard to others.

name: VET - Student American Veterinary Medical Association at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The objectives of the Cornell University SAVMA shall be as follow: a.	To foster a united school spirit and to provide support of issues for the benefit of students within the college; b.	To provide opportunities for members to gain additional professional knowledge and an understanding of professional ethics; c.	To provide the students the benefits offered by the American Veterinary Medical Association to its student chapters and the advantages of belonging to a professional organization; d.	To support, facilitate, and encourage student, faculty, and administration involvement in activities of benefit to the overall personal and professional growth of the general student body; e.	To develop the characteristics of leadership through training received in conducting the Cornell University SAVMA's affairs; f.	To foster and maintain relations between the students, college, university, surrounding community, New York State Veterinary Medical Society, American Veterinary Medical Association.

name: VET - Student Chapter of the National Association for Black Veterinarians at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The mission of NABV is to "advocate, provide support, and cultivate an inclusive community for Blacks in veterinary medicine at every level of the profession through the organization, members and leadership." The purpose of the chapter is to provide support and community to Black students at CUCVM, to maintain strong relationships with Black alumni, and to offer opportunities for Black and minority pre-veterinary students to better understand the field.

name: VET - Student Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Society
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: SVECCS is a student organization designed to promote the education and involvement of veterinary students in emergency and critical care medicine.

name: VET - Surgery Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: This club seeks to provide veterinary students with additional exposure to the world of veterinary surgery through lectures, wet labs, workshops, and other activities.

name: VET - Tabletop Vets
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Tabletop Games, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Tabletop Vets is a graduate/professional school organization founded to foster an environment in which all members of the Cornell Community may safely gather to play tabletop games. Members play a variety of games, including board-, card-, and pen & paper- games, in a setting which encourages social interaction and positive mental well-being.

name: VET - The Association of Asian Veterinary Medical Professionals at Cornell
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: 1. Provide professional and educational resources to AAPI veterinary professionals, veterinary students, and clients. 2. Encourage an interest in veterinary medicine among AAPI youth and support aspiring AAPI veterinary professionals through providing mentorship and other educational resources. 3. Facilitate networking opportunities among AAPI veterinary professionals. 4. Collaborate with similarly aligned diversity initiatives and affinity groups to advocate for greater general diversity in the veterinary profession.

name: VET - Theriogenology Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Student Chapter of the Society for Theriogenology is an organization for students who are interested in the study of reproduction in animals. In particular, it hopes to acquaint the student with the varying aspects of reproduction as it pertains to veterinary medicine - disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, surgery, research, and related fields.

name: VET - Ultrasound A Cappella
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Ultrasound brings together vet students to sing, perform and arrange both traditional and modern music in a mixed voices, non-auditioned group. We collaborate with the vet college's Dance Collective and musical theatre group, Vet Players, and perform yearly for the vet school and for the Cornell community.

name: VET - Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of Veterinarians as One Inclusive Community for Empowerment (VOICE) is: 1. To increase awareness, respect and sensitivity to differences among all individuals and communities in the field of veterinary medicine These include, but are not limited to, sex, race, color, age, national origin, religion, disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity/reassignment, gender expression, citizenship, pregnancy or parental status, veteran or military status, and educational background 2. To celebrate diversity within the profession of veterinary medicine and provide a campus environment that embraces diversity and promotes the success of students, particularly underrepresented students 3. To promote the importance of cross-cultural awareness in veterinary medicine in order to meet the needs of our diversifying clientele 4. To promote the veterinary profession, provide leadership and mentorship to any youth, particularly underrepresented youth, interested in careers in veterinary medicine

name: VET - Veterinary Business Management Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Veterinary Business Management Association is a student-driven organization dedicated to advancing the profession through increasing business knowledge, creating networking opportunities, and empowering students to achieve their personal and professional goals.

name: VET - Veterinary Education Club
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: Cornell's Veterinary Education Club aims to serve our Student Body through events and activities that enhance student wellness while also integrating our students into the local community. We work with the Office of Student Academic Services to promote relevant programming, and we also coordinate with other organizations to promote events related to student wellness. The Veterinary Education Club also focuses on educating the local community about current veterinary issues via outreach programs. We work with local 4-H clubs, the undergraduate Pre-Veterinary Society, and this year we will be working with some of the local elementary schools.  This is a fantastic outlet for current veterinary students who are interested in becoming involved in academia, clinical instruction, and/or public outreach.

name: VET - Veterinary Internal Medicine the Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of the Chapter is to promote the specialties of cardiology, neurology, oncology, large animal internal medicine, and small animal internal medicine through the advancement of knowledge to veterinary medical students.

name: VET - Veterinary Medicine Open House
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine Open House organization is committed to the planning, organization, set up, and management of the annual Vet School Open House.

name: VET - Veterinary One Health Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The objectives of the organization are as follows: 1) to provide veterinary students with educational opportunities in the one health aspects of veterinary medicine; 2) to aid in the career development of students by informing them of the opportunities available in the one and public health sector; 3) to enhance leadership characteristics and skills; 4) to increase awareness of disease and biosecurity as it pertains to food safety, environmental health animal health, and public health; and 5) to host an annual Veterinary One Health Symposium.

name: VET - Veterinary Players
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of The Vet Players is to foster creativity among veterinary students and provide a creative outlet for exploration. The organization promotes communication, community, and creativity by putting on theatrical events and productions throughout the academic year.

name: VET - Veterinary Radiology Club at Cornell University
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of the Cornell University Veterinary Radiology Club is to promote and encourage the study of radiology and other diagnostic imaging modalities by exploring all aspects of diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy through presentations, learning modules, and hands- on experience. Diagnostic imaging modalities include: small and large animal diagnostic radiology, diagnostic ultrasound, nuclear medicine, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging.

name: VET - Wildlife Disease Association Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The objectives of the Student Chapters of the Wildlife Disease Association include the mission of the WDA, and more specifically aim to educating students interested in wildlife health and disease about the profession, career opportunities, job qualifications, externship opportunities. We also aim to enhance the skills of these students through lectures, workshops, conferences, and field trips. Finally, by connecting students interested in wildlife health and disease to mentors in WDA, networking is one of our main objectives.

name: VET - Women's Veterinary Leadership Development Initiative Student Chapter
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, PROF: Science/Healthcare, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to achieve leadership excellence in every sector of veterinary medicine that fully reflects the diversity of the profession and society. This organization shall support women in seeking and achieving leadership, policy, and decision-making positions within all areas of professional veterinary activity. This organization shall provide support and opportunities for students to learn leadership skills, and develop mentoring relationships

name: VET - World Aquatic Veterinary Medical Association
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The Mission of the Chapter is to provide Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine students with information on aquatic veterinary educational, career and other opportunities, and to develop programs useful for the World Aquatic Veterinary Medical Association to help increase the knowledge, skills and involvement of veterinary students at CUCVM, and elsewhere, in aquatic veterinary medicine.

name: VET - Zoo and Wildlife Society
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, Sustainability/Environmental, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: The purpose of the Zoo and Wildlife Society (ZAWS) is to expose veterinary students and the larger Cornell community to the care and veterinary treatment of animals outside of the standard veterinary curriculum.

name: VET- Dawghouse FC
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, AFFILIATION: College of Veterinary Medicine
description: As students of the College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM), we know first hand that there is a lot of work and pressure constantly being pushed onto us. We want to create a space where we can relieve some of that stress through soccer! Soccer is a fantastic way to run off steam, have fun exercising, engage in healthy competition, and meet new people. Our intent for developing this club is not only to provide an outlet from school work, but to also help develop soccer skills, teamwork, and confidence in a fun and safe environment. The club is open to all who want to play soccer, both undergraduate and graduate students, with the idea that the grad students can also help mentor the undergrads in a less formal environment. The Dawgs are looking forward to playing on campus year-round, both indoors and out. We hope you can join us!

name: Women's Management Council
category: Grad/Professional University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson School, PROF: Business and Management
description: The Women's Management Council sponsors efforts to increase the enrollment of women within the Johnson School, influences the environment around us to promote and support women in business, provides a structure for connecting with present and future women leaders, and supports the diverse professional and personal aspirations of women within our community.

name: 302 Wait Avenue Co-op
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: We are a cooperative living house on north campus that cares for one another and promotes a safe living space for women and non-binary identifying people.

name: 660 Stewart Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, International/Multicultural, Sustainability/Environmental, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: The purpose of 660 shall be to provide quality housing, or rather a home to its members, by promoting the concept of cooperative living in accordance with the spirit of the Rochdale Principles of Cooperation.

name: Actuarial Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: Our club aims to provide awareness for the actuarial profession and to assist those striving to become an actuary by strengthening their leadership, networking, professional, and actuarial skills.

name: After Eight A Cappella
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: After Eight's purpose is to entertain audiences at Cornell and elsewhere while providing women and gender minorities the chance to perform contemporary music a cappella.

name: Agua Clara
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: AguaClara Cornell is a student-led program that develops and implements sustainable, gravity-powered water treatment technologies to bring safe water on tap to communities around the world.

name: Air and Sea Hospitality
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: This organization explores the airline and cruise industry as a whole and exposes members to the various opportunities that exist within the businesses. We provide resources to help you learn more about the industry and build the knowledge and network to work in it.

name: ALANA Intercultural Programming Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AY27 - Byline
description: We seek to provide the Cornell community with wide and diversified programming on a regular basis as well as allocate funds to registered student organizations for programs that encourage diversity and intercultural efforts.

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Business and Management
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is Cornell University's Original Co-Ed Professional Business Fraternity dedicated to providing a professional and social environment in which its brothers can thrive. Founded in 1904, Alpha Kappa Psi is the nation's oldest professional business fraternity as well. Our chapter at Cornell University was founded in 1998 and is one of over 190 College Chapters across the nation, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We host and engage in a variety of professional, social, and philanthropic activities that help develop experienced and ethical leaders and foster life-long bonds and memories. Today, as always, the Omicron Upsilon chapter is dedicated to furthering the individual welfare of its members and the community.

name: Alzheimer's Buddies
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Alzheimer's Buddies at Cornell is a student-led organization aimed at overcoming the social disengagement experienced by those affected by intermediate-to-late-stages of Alzheimer's Disease. The purpose of this organization is to pair students to volunteer 1-on-1 with dementia residents, build social skills as well as raise awareness through participating in fundraisers and hosting talks on current advancements in Alzheimer's Disease research.

name: American Hotel and Lodging Association Student Chapter at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: The purpose of the chapter is to be the primary advocates of the American lodging industry for SHA students through education, information and member services, and to build meaningful and professional connections between the American Hotel and Lodging Association and Cornell University. Our main goals are as follows: 1.	To provide members opportunities to exchange ideas, strategies, and contacts with industry leaders at any of AH&LA events throughout the year. 2.	To educate members on the latest industry trend and research through AH&LA online information services. 3.	To expose new members to different aspects of hospitality business through hotel tours in New York City. 4.	To assist members to achieve their career goals through AH&LA's career services and network. 5.	To assist the local community through community service events. 6.	To provide our members with professional development opportunities with the help of fellow students, alumni, faculty, and industry professionals.

name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The primary vision of Cornell University's AISES chapter is the development of a new generation of educated Native leaders who will in turn contemplate, study, and contribute to the building of a Nation and community among Native Americans.

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE) at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: We are Cornell's student chapter of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE), a national network of chemical engineering professionals and students.  Our chapter's mission is to strengthen the Cornell ChemE community and enrich the ChemE undergraduate experience through professional, outreach, and social programming.

name: American Meteorological Society at Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Sustainability/Environmental
description: We are Cornell Weather. Our mission is to encourage the pursuit of meteorological knowledge on Cornell's campus and create a community within the Atmospheric Science department. We also seek to introduce undergraduates to various professional opportunities in the Atmospheric Sciences and facilitate research, and help them work on skills crucial to the science in ways that help the Cornell community at large.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers at Cornell University Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: Cornell ASME aims to enrich the lives of students of the Sibley School by providing professional and social networking events, information about post-graduation career paths, and local outreach activities. We uphold the ASME mission to serve diverse global communities by advancing, disseminating and applying engineering knowledge for improving the quality of life, and communicating the excitement of engineering.

name: Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: The mission of Animal Science: Mentoring Our Undergraduates is to foster mentorship between current Animal Science students and incoming Animal Science students with hopes to ease the transition into the program and build a community of students that spans generations.

name: AppDev at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: The philosophy of Cornell AppDev is to curate a tight-knit, inclusive community where any person can be part of the process to solve problems through app development. We do this by building apps using industry-level techniques with an emphasis on mobile development, cultivating a strong mentorship culture, and educating the next generation of Cornellians in our craft.

name: Applied & Engineering Physics Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of this organization is to develop a strong and welcoming undergraduate culture in the Applied & Engineering Physics department. This group will create an infrastructure for undergraduates interested in or affiliated with A&EP to both act as and seek academic mentors, spend more time with A&EP peers in a social setting, participate in outreach events to encourage undergraduates to join the A&EP major, and to facilitate communication between the undergraduate community and the A&EP department faculty. The A&EP Society intends additionally to provide opportunities for members to explore the applications of studying A&EP outside of the theoretical knowledge gained in the classroom.

name: Aprendizaje Liderazgo Motivacion Autoestima
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: ALMA exists to:  Build community among Latina and non-binary identifying students.  Provide professional and personal development through mentorship, networking, and leadership opportunities.  Coordinate and host events, social convenings, and cultural programming as voted and approved by the ALMA board via quorum.  Advocate for and amplify the voices of Latina and non-binary students across campus.

name: Army ROTC Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The Army ROTC Club at Cornell University provides leadership development within the framework of the Army Values, while promoting Equality, Fraternity, and Liberty within Cornell Leadership development efforts. In addition, the Army ROTC Club will impart education and outreach regarding Cornell's military history and achievements.

name: Art Beyond Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Visual Arts
description: Art Beyond Cornell aims to bring new perspectives to both Cornell students and institutionalized youth in the Tompkins County area by providing a means of connection, self-expression, communication, growth, and joy through art.

name: ASL @ Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: ASL @ Cornell aims to promote heightened awareness of and appreciation for American Sign Language (ASL) and Deaf culture in collaboration with Cornell’s ASL/Deaf Studies program. In doing so, we hope to cultivate an inclusive environment on campus and in the city of Ithaca that welcomes Deaf and hard of hearing individuals while allowing all students to develop a greater understanding of ASL and encouraging them to apply their classroom knowledge to the community.

name: Association for Engagement and Partnership
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The mission of the Association for Students and Community is to increase the recruitment and retention of students within the College of Human Ecology.

name: Association of Computer Science Undergraduates
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The Association of Computer Science Undergraduates (ACSU) promotes educational, professional, and social interaction among every undergraduate student interested in computer science.

name: AutoBoat at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell AutoBoat aims to push the boundaries of novel maritime technology by designing, manufacturing, and testing an autonomous boat capable of image recognition, complex path planning, and interacting with its environment.

name: Autonomous Sailboat Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The goal of CUSail is to design and manufacture a small, cheap, and mass-producible autonomous robotic sailboat that can intelligently navigate any body of water and collect data. The project is meant to decrease environmental research and acoustic marine mammal monitoring costs by designing a research vessel that can cheaply collect data.

name: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The Cornell University Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (CUAUV) team designs and builds AUVs for competition and research. CUAUV competes annually in the RoboSub Competition, hosted by the AUVSI Foundation and Office of Naval Research in San Diego, California.

name: Baja Racing at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Cornell Baja Racing shall be to design and build an off-road vehicle each year to compete in the Baja SAE Collegiate Design Series competition. The organization provides hands-on engineering, teamwork, and leadership experience to its diverse members from all backgrounds.

name: Best Buddies at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Best Buddies is a nonprofit organization dedicated to establishing a global volunteer movement that creates opportunities for one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, and leadership development for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD).

name: Big Red Ambassadors
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: Big Red Ambassadors is a university club in which Cornell students, under the guidance of the Undergraduate Admissions Office work as liaisons between current students and prospective students. Big Red Ambassadors participate in University information sessions, responding to general student-life questions emailed to admissions, lead our Cornell Days program (a special on-campus program for admitted students), and in general, are a primary resource for prospective students and their families.

name: Big Red Bears
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: A student organization aimed to increase school spirit through the use of the Cornell mascot, Touchdown the Big Red Bear. We work to bring Touchdown to every Cornell athletic event and every university event for which we are requested, along with certain requested private events. We also train new students to become Touchdown and ensure that his legacy and spirit can continue to be passed on to Cornellians past, present, and future.

name: Big Red Buddies
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Our mission is to engage interested Cornell undergraduates with the Ithaca community by providing weekly volunteering opportunities at the Head Start Centers in Ithaca.  Our focus is on emphasizing the importance of early childhood development and allowing Cornell students to use their skills to foster relationships with the younger students of our community, with a focus on working with underserved children.

name: Big Red Marching Band
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The objective of the BRMB is to foster an inclusive and open environment where all band members feel welcome and comfortable regardless of any identity a member may hold. The primary functions of the Big Red Bands are to promote school spirit, support the activities of Cornell athletics, and provide musical and visual entertainment to the Ithaca community.

name: Big Red Pep Band at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of the Big Red Pep Band is to provide musical entertainment and promote school spirit at Cornell and elsewhere. The Pep Band is responsible for attending all Men's home hockey games while classes are in session, along with as many other athletic contests as possible.

name: BigRed/Hacks
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: BigRed//Hacks is Cornell's collegiate hackathon. During the academic year, we also hold workshops and events for the Cornell community.

name: Biomedical Device at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Biomedical Device at Cornell (CUBMD) is a team of multidisciplinary undergraduate students formed under a shared interest for biomedical device innovation with the ultimate goal of advancing healthcare. Our mission is to identify contemporary problems in the field of biomedical devices, design and innovate solutions to said problems, and work to bring our solutions to the market where they can have the most widespread, positive impact.

name: Black Bio-medical and Technical Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: This organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University.
