category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: CUPB inspires and enriches the Cornell experience by bringing artists and events that involve, excite and entertain the community.

name: Custom Silicon Systems at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Silicon CMOS chips are at the heart of every modern computing device from the smallest Internet-of Things (IoT) device to the largest supercomputer. Unfortunately, undergraduate students currently do not have any opportunity to actually go through the process of fully specifying, designing, implementing, testing, fabricating, and evaluating a computer chip. Undergraduates leave Cornell thinking that fabricating computer chips is only possible at huge companies like Intel, AMD, NVIDIA and Apple. Until recently, there was no realistic hands-on way for students to, experience the complete computer chip design process. At the same time, exposing students to the beauty of computer chip design has never been more important, since the slowing of CMOS technology scaling means computer system designers must increasingly rely on specialized computer chips for continued improvements in performance and/or energy efficiency. How can students (from freshmen to seniors) gain hands-on computer chip design experience? The answer lies in the recent explosion in open-source chip design tools, open-source chip implementations, open-source process design kits, and low-cost computer chip fabrication services. Just as open-source software has democratized software design, open-source hardware is poised to democratized hardware design. In addition to open source hardware, changes in IP control regulations have enabled students to utilize older, commercial design kits. Universities are also uniquely poised to access cutting-edge commercial design tools, enabling student-led designs to be made with these ever more accessible design kits. Due to a combination of both the accessibility of open-source, and the power of industry tools, IC design has never before been so available to interested undergraduates. The Cornell Custom Silicon Systems (C2S2) Project Team is a new project team traditionally funded through the Shen Fund for Social Impact, as well as commercial (AMD, Cadence, Marvell, Amazon Annapurna Labs) and government (Sandia National Labs, NORDTECH) sponsorships. The team is leveraging this emerging open and closed-source hardware ecosystems to enable undergraduate students to specify, design, implement, test, fabricate, and evaluate custom computer chips. The final outcome will be a custom computer chip integrated on a custom circuit board with a complete software stack targeting an important application domain. This ambitious student-led team is likely unique across US universities, and will hopefully inspire a new generation of computer system designers.

name: Data Science Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: Current initiatives range from devising a scalable mapping system for better natural disaster response to developing a tool that can summarize Amazon reviews for a better user experience. Our team of 70+ students is a great place to meet people with diverse interests, gain experience at the intersection of theory and application, and contribute to the greater community initiatives.

name: Design by Biomedical Undergraduate Teams (DEBUT) at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Cornell DEBUT is an engineering project team working to develop innovative solutions for current biomedical needs. After two years of in-depth research and development, our biomedical device prototype is submitted to the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIBIB) and VentureWell's Design by Biomedical Undergraduate Teams (DEBUT) competition, where it is judged on innovation, marketability, and patentability.

name: Dietetics Association at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The mission of the Cornell University Dietetic Association is to (1) create and maintain a network and sense of community among Cornell dietetics students, faculty, staff, and alumni as well as facilitate a strong relationship with student, state, and national dietetic associations; (2) explore/raise awareness of dietetics education and internships.

name: Digital Tech & Innovation
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell Digital Tech & Innovation (DTI) makes community impact through technology. We create websites, mobile apps, and community-based initiatives to create positive experiences for people at Cornell and beyond. We foster our personal growth and teach others while always being professional, open-minded, and inclusive.

name: Dilmun Hill Student Farm
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Food/Drink, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Dilmun Hill is a student-run farm at Cornell University that fosters community and empowers students through active engagement in ecological agriculture, research and outreach and provides opportunities for experiential learning.

name: DREAM Team at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: DREAM Team exists to promote the common value and shared community standard of "any person, any study" by empowering undocumented students through advising and providing a support network. We aim to expand awareness and acceptance in the local community through advocacy and educational outreach.

name: Dyson Undergraduate Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Dyson School
description: The Dyson Undergraduate Council is a student-directed organization committed to promoting and strengthening the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management. The organization consists of students with diverse backgrounds and experiences, all united by their passion for the Dyson School community and undergraduate Applied Economics and Management (AEM) major.

name: EARS - Empathy Assistance and Referral Service
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Health/Wellbeing, AY27 - Byline
description: Founded in 1972, EARS (Empathy, Assistance & Referral Service) is a student-led organization that promotes mental health and well-being for everyone in the Cornell community, including undergraduate and graduate students, staff, and faculty.

name: Electric Vehicles at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: To foster a collaborative environment where students can share knowledge, continually innovate, and develop professional skills by engineering a highly-efficient autonomous electric vehicle.

name: Emergency Medical Service at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, AY27 - Byline
description: Cornell University Emergency Medical Service (CUEMS) strives to provide professional, efficient, and effective first-response basic life support care to the Ithaca campus and surrounding areas. Serving Cornell students, faculty, staff, visitors, and their families, CUEMS responds to all 911 calls for medical assistance twenty-four hours a day, seven days per week during the academic year. CUEMS provides extensive, weekly training to all squad members consisting of New York State certified emergency medical technicians. Moreover, CUEMS offers training to the entire Cornell community in cardiopulmonary resuscitation, automated external defibrillation, first aid, and activation of emergency medical services. Working together with other emergency services from Cornell University and Tompkins County, CUEMS provides a valuable resource to the Ithaca campus and much of the surrounding Tompkins County community.

name: Encouraging Young Engineers and Scientists
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Major budget cuts in the Ithaca school district have left young students without exposure to fun and exciting science enrichment activities. EYES aims to fulfill this need in the Ithaca community by bringing engaging science and engineering activities to the Ithaca elementary schools in order to encourage young students to consider careers in STEM fields.

name: ENG - American Society of Civil Engineers
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The objective of ASCE shall be to encourage the development of a professional consciousness, to afford an opportunity for civil and environmental engineering students to become acquainted and to practice working together effectively, to promote a spirit of congeniality among them, and to provide friendly contact with the engineering professions.

name: ENG - Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: "Our mission is to represent and elevate the professional standing of the Asian heritage community of STEM students at Cornell University by providing a community for professional development, opportunities, and resources. By providing these opportunities to our members we aim to create a community where our members have a chance to further their career and strive to build a vibrant community that fosters social, cultural, and professional connections while promoting mutual professional and interpersonal growth and support among our members."

name: Engineering World Health at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The purpose of Cornell Engineering World Health shall be to create meaningful impact through innovative technology solutions that target the world’s most pressing health issues.

name: Engineers for a Sustainable World
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Engineers for a Sustainable World - Cornell University Project Team works to forge innovative changes in sustainability technology and education. Our students are empowered to challenge barriers to sustainable living around the world. ESW follows the mission statement of ESW-Global, which is as follows: “We strive to empower students and professionals to tackle sustainability challenges. We work towards a sustainable world supported by a network of passionate engineers. Our goals are as follows: 1. Design and implement hands-on sustainability projects across the globe. 2. Educate students and practicing engineers on sustainability best practices. 3. Unite those passionate about sustainability in a productive international network.”

name: Engineers in Action
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: Engineers in Action empowers today's students to become tomorrow's global leaders by building bridges and WASH systems with underserved communities. We envision a world in which global citizens connect across cultures to improve quality of life and ensure geography doesn't determine access to opportunity.

name: Engineers Without Borders Cornell University Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Our mission is to partner with communities around the world to design and implement sustainable, community-driven engineering solutions. We strive to build strong, long-lasting relationships grounded in mutual respect, cultural understanding, and local empowerment. As students, we gain hands-on experience in responsible engineering practice—balancing technical design with cultural, environmental, and economic considerations. Through this work, we develop a deeper understanding of global challenges, resource limitations, and the importance of equity and sustainability in engineering.

name: Environmental Collaborative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: ECO (Environmental Collaborative) is a student organization that works to unite on-campus student groups toward environmental, sustainable, and ecologically focused initiatives. We commit fully to the following: 1. To increase dialogue amongst environmental organizations and all other interested organizations, 2. To launch and uphold meaningful venues for reducing negative environmental impact and upholding social justice and to provide opportunities for all students to gain knowledge and experience in relevant issues, 3. To provide support to and information for existing environmental initiatives, and 4. To foster meaningful relationships with Cornell’s administration and the Ithaca community.

name: Fantastic Fungi Fanatics
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The Fantastic Fungi Fanatics club creates a platform for people to share their passion for fungi. Fungi are often overlooked in our surroundings but play an essential role in our everyday lives and in all ecosystems. Our club activities may include but are not limited to: o	Mushroom hunting field trips o	Experimental exploration -Mushroom identification -Mushroom cultivation -Cooking with mushrooms -Discussions on research and studies -Others (slime molds, fermentation, etc.) o	Movie nights o	Shroom art (spore prints, etc.) Our goal is to create a fun and stimulating environment to dig in to the field of mycology. We want to spread our zest for mushrooms with the Cornell and Ithaca communities!

name: First Generation Student Union
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The First Gen Student Union aims to promote community, resources, advocacy, and empowerment for all students who identify with the first-generation and/or low-income student experience. We consider you a first-generation college student if you come from a family in which neither of your parents or guardians has obtained a four-year college degree. We consider you a low-income student if you have little or no expected parent contribution as part of your financial aid package, you are a recipient of the Pell grant, or you believe that your prior academic and social experiences have been limited due to your socioeconomic status.

name: Food Science Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Food/Drink
description: The purpose of Food Science Club shall be to foster a close relationship among the Food Science students and faculty at Cornell University; to encourage leadership and acquaint students with the scope of food science and technology; to spread awareness of food science to the Cornell University and larger Ithaca community; to provide members with opportunities to engage with the professional food industry.

name: Food Science Product Development Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Food/Drink
description: The purpose of this organization is to foster excellence and education among Cornell students who are interested in product development.

name: Friends of Farmworkers
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Friends of Farmworkers was founded to provide consistent ESL instruction to area farmworkers who know little or no English.

name: FSAE Racing at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Cornell Racing FSAE shall be to design, manufacture and compete a vehicle according to the rules and regulations of the Formula SAE competition.

name: Gender Justice Advocacy Coalition
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The Gender Justice Advocacy Coalition (GJAC) is a byline-funded student organization committed to justice and advocacy for all genders. We operate out of an intersectional and global lens with a focus on gender-marginalized folks. We aim to encourage meaningful and critical conversations related to the gendered lived experiences of all people. We seek to foster relationships with campus partners in order to support and amplify the work of Cornell social justice organizations through funding, awareness-raising, and advocacy.

name: Glee Club, Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The oldest student run organization on Cornell's campus, the Glee Club strives to bring choral music to the world through performances on and off campus.  Rehearsals are held twice a week in Sage Chapel.  Notable events include a winter tour (both national and international), and the Homecoming concert as well as collaborations with orchestras for the presentation of major works.  The Glee Club also serves as the torch bearers of the traditional Cornell Songs.

name: Global Action Impact Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: GAIA maximizes the positive impact for communities in need by empowering college teams to conceive, design, prototype, and execute solutions for global sustainability.

name: Global Development Student Advisory Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services
description: The mission of the Global Development Student Advisory Board is to build a community of students who possess a passion for uniting critical scholarship and practice at the intersections of agricultural, environmental, life, and social sciences, to advance a more equitable, sustainable, and food-secure world for all. Side-by-side with our diverse network of global and community partners, we demonstrate our commitment to inclusion, innovation, and furthering the study and practice of global development. We embrace a transdisciplinary approach that emphasizes real-world engagement on a global scale — with communities in New York State, across the United States, and around the world.  Board members include students interested in a variety of related career fields, who are eager to work as an interdisciplinary team.  Board members serve as a voice for students in the department of Global Development, relaying student wishes and desires regarding curriculum, advisement, and other department initiatives.

name: Global Health Student Advisory Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: The Global Health Student Advisory Board (GHSAB) is a student-led board that works in collaboration with the DNS Global Health Program. The GHSAB develops and improves global and public health programming that engages students, faculty, staff, and alumni across the university. Through our unequivocal passion for global and public health, we aim to increase awareness of global and public health issues while promoting health equity, diversity, and inclusion. As a diverse group of students—representing different races, ethnicities, geographies, genders, majors, and professional aspirations—we all hold unique worldviews that inform our global health programming. We are committed to shifting the discourse on Cornell's campus to promote racial justice, health equity, and responsible engagement with diverse communities by hosting several opportunities and events throughout the academic year.

name: GreenClub
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: To create a community enabling anyone to act on climate chnage.

name: Guild of Visual Arts
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Visual Arts
description: The Guild of Visual Arts exists to give artists of any skill level a strong on-campus community where they can develop their skills in a positive group setting. The Guild of Visual Arts aims to connect individuals with artistic interests with one another and provide a forum for members to share their ideas and skills!

name: Hack4Impact
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: We collaborate with nonprofits and other socially responsible organizations to develop software that meets important social and humanitarian needs.

name: Haven: The LGBTQ Student Union
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: Haven: The LGBTQ Student Union seeks to enrich Cornell University by supporting its diverse array of sexual and gender identities and expressions. Through education, outreach, and service, we promote understanding and the development of inclusive communities. Haven serves as an administrative umbrella for most of the undergraduate (though generally open to graduate and professional students as well) student organizations involved in the support and outreach to LGBTQ students at Cornell. Haven provides a vehicle for these groups to secure funding and on-going training, and consultation with professional staff. Haven collaborates with other Cornell groups to address the social support needs of students.

name: History of Art Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Visual Arts
description: HART Club seeks to cultivate an understanding of art history as a field and career among Cornellians and work to foster a deeper appreciation for art, artists, and art historians by providing the community with opportunities to engage directly with art and art history.

name: Hortus Forum - Undergraduate Horticulture Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: Cultivating a positive social community which fosters a passion for plants and teaches the value of horticulture. Hortus Forum has a key role in providing educational experiences beyond the classroom and teaching the Cornell community about plants.  This includes but is not limited to: field trips, presentations and workshops, promotion of internships, career development opportunities, and social events. Plant sales are a necessary function of the organization; they are a means of generating revenue, and are utilized as learning opportunities and outreach. Although plant sales primarily encompass ornamental plants, Hortus Forum represents the breadth horticulture and includes opportunities for engaging with a diversity of plant-based experiences.

name: Hospitality Asset Managers Association, Cornell University Student Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: The Hospitality Asset Managers Association Club at Cornell University aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice in hospitality asset management. Our purpose is to enrich our members' understanding and capabilities through engaging educational programs, guest lectures from industry leaders, and hands-on opportunities. We strive to cultivate a community of aspiring professionals equipped with the knowledge and skills to excel in the dynamic field of hospitality asset management.

name: Hotel Ezra Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: Hotel Ezra Cornell (HEC) is a weekend-long business conference organized and executed by the students of the School of Hotel Administration. The conference boasts a series of educational seminars, food and beverage events, and leisure activities to generate thought-provoking conversation about the industry and build long-term relationships between current and future hospitality professionals. A 102-year-old tradition of the school, HEC allows students to practice the skills they have learned in the classroom and showcase their talents to industry leaders, supporting the program's mission of "Showcasing Hospitality Education Through Student Leadership."

name: Hotel Sales and Marketing Association International Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: HSMAI operates as part of a greater international organization, boasting memebrs from numerous universities and companies around the globe.

name: Hotel Society, Collegiate Chapter
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: The Cornell Hotel Society, Collegiate Chapter (CHS,CC) is dedicated to supporting the Nolan Hotel School students and their interests through the promotion of active involvement in student organizations by coordinating school wide events and networking opportunities with our alumni. All students of the Nolan Hotel School, graduate and undergraduate, attain membership upon matriculation. CHS, CC works closely with the Cornell Hotel Society (CHS) Global Chapter to maintain the connection between the alumni and the students at the Nolan Hotel School.

name: iGEM at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Cornell Genetically Engineered Machines (iGEM) is an award-winning synthetic biology research team comprised of over 50 undergraduate students in five subteams: Wet Lab, Product Development, Policy and Practices, Business, and Wiki/Design. Using techniques in genetic engineering, the team develops projects that address local and global problems related to medical applications, environmental concerns, and human and animal health. Each year, the team competes with over 450 multidisciplinary teams from all around the world at the iGEM Grand Jamboree, currently hosted in Paris, France, hosted by the International Genetically Engineered Machine Foundation.

name: ILR Student Government Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Student Groups for Student Services
description: To actively and aggressively represent the undergraduate population of the ILR School and Cornell University through education, programming, and any activities that will enhance the educational circumstances of the ILR School.

name: Information Science Student Association - Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: As the Information Science Student Association (ISSA) we are open to all students (majors, minors, or undeclared) interested in Information Science or Information Science, Systems, & Technology. The Information Science Student Association is here to improve the student experience and spread the word about our fast-growing and cutting-edge major. Our club plans networking events, social events, corporate information sessions, and meet-and-greets with Cornell faculty.

name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell IEEE seeks to serve the ECE community through professional networking events including company information sessions and industry recruitment events as well as social and academic gatherings to better unite ECE students.

name: Interfaith Council at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Spiritual/Religious, AY27 - Byline
description: The Cornell Interfaith Council seeks to promote interfaith dialogue and support religious life on campus, while encouraging shared understanding and celebration of our differences.

name: Interfraternity Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, Community Service
description: The self-governing body for the 33 recognized Interfraternity Council fraternities at Cornell.  Creates policies, oversees the judicial process, and plans programming and initiatives for the community.  Has a 9 person elected IFC Exec Board.

name: International Students Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, AY27 - Byline
description: The recently rechristened International Students Association (ISA), previously the International Students Union (ISU) and International Students Board (ISB) is an organization of students from a diverse background committed to promoting dialogue and awareness about world events, cultures and issues. We fulfill this goal through the ISA's original events and the funding of student organizations, as well as assisting in the planning and execution of their events. The ISA believes that the university environment offers a unique opportunity for the interaction of ideas and opinions. The prestige and resources of Cornell University allow us to plan major events and to hear from influential speakers, and we are committed to fulfilling this potential. Further, the ISA encourages all student groups to approach the Board with ideas and suggestions concerning events or speakers they would like to see on campus. The International Students Association is also committed to student advocacy, focusing on issues that affect international and diverse students. These projects can be in response to long-term concerns, current global events, or changes in policies by the university's administration. The ISA does not take any political stance on issues but we support the right of student organizations to present these issues to the Cornell Community.

name: JazzPlus
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: JazzPlus encourages its members to carry on the deeply rooted histories and traditions of jazz, while simultaneously augmenting them through inspiration from other genres. While many members of the organization participate in department jazz ensembles, JazzPlus is open to everyone. JazzPlus presents workshops and clinics to musicians and listeners of the Cornell and Ithaca communities. Topics of discussion may include but are not limited to: jazz style, technique, composition, fundamentals, improvisation, history, culture, and performance. JazzPlus will sponsor a lecture series with guest artists from outside of the area as well as from the local community. JazzPlus will also facilitate musical events to provide the Cornell and surrounding communities with the opportunity to appreciate jazz by participating as performers and as spectators. Events may include but are not limited to: regular jazz-related social events, jam sessions and concerts on campus, publicizing JazzPlus and Cornell University Jazz Ensemble performances, and promotion of other jazz events on and off campus.

name: La Asociación Latina
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: La Asociación Latina has an objective as of 1975, we the Latinx Students at Cornell University have united with the intent to create a collective organization that will serve as a forum to address the social, cultural, political and educational concerns of the Latinx community at Cornell University.

name: Language Expansion Program
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Through weekly peer-led Language Corners, the Language Expansion Program provides a cooperative and encouraging environment for students to practice their target languages and exchange cultural knowledge. We foster language proficiency and cultural empathy within the Cornell community, with the goal that members will better serve their communities through translation and interpreting.

name: Liquid Propulsion at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: Our goal is to help Cornell students develop relevant skills and expertise in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Business Operations through our team’s technical projects focused on experimental rocket and jet propulsion research and development.

name: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Publication/Media, Political/Speech/Debate
description: Logos: The Cornell Undergraduate Philosophy Club and Journal is a refereed journal at the Sage School of Philosophy in Ithaca, New York. An entirely student-run journal, Logos publishes undergraduate work in all branches and traditions of philosophy. Undergraduates from around the globe are invited to submit papers annually for peer-review. Accepted papers are published in the current year's edition of Logos, and the authors of the top three submissions are awarded cash prizes. In addition to publishing the journal, Logos functions as the general-interest philosophical club for the undergraduate student body. Logos sponsors reading and discussion groups, lectures, debates, and social events. Students of all backgrounds are welcome and encouraged to join.

name: Mars Rover at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Our student-run team fosters creativity and intellectual growth through the development of our rover. As engineers, we strive to cultivate a creative environment where brilliant young minds can develop innovative, intellectual, and leadership qualities through our vision of building a rover that may one day aid in the exploration of the final frontier.

name: Minds Matter at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Health/Wellbeing, AY27 - Byline
description: Cornell Minds Matter (CMM) promotes mental health awareness and emotional well-being for all Cornell students. We work to reduce the stigma of mental illness by holding educational events and creating safe spaces to foster a healthy, balanced lifestyle. CMM acts as a liaison between students, faculty, staff, and administration to advocate for the student perspective on mental health resources and campus policies. Through our project teams and G-Body members, we continue to provide accessible resources that serve the needs of our diverse living-learning community. Whether your interests stem from personal experiences, academic goals, a desire for social action, or curiosity, we welcome you to join us on our mission. We all have mental health- spend your time at Cornell prioritizing yours! Cornell Minds Matter is a Student Assembly Byline Organization.

name: Minority Industrial and Labor Relations Student Organization
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Business and Management
description: The Minority ILR Student Organization (MILRSO) provides social, academic, and pre-professional support to its members. Open to all students, MILRSO facilitates a cross-cultural dialogue that addresses the experiences of underrepresented identities in the workplace. MILRSO maintains corporate and alumni contacts to aid members' professional development. For MILRSO, underrepresented identities include: people of color, the LGBTQ community, non-conforming persons, women, or gender. MILRSO exists as a place for these communities to feel welcome and to feel supported.

name: Mosaic Hospitality Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: The purpose of Mosaic Hospitality Association shall be to provide education, leadership training, mentorship, and customized support to encourage the full mosaic of hospitality talent in building meaningful careers and lasting economic opportunity for all.

name: Multicultural Community-Fueled Activities Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The purpose of MCFAB shall be to bring performers of color to the Cornell campus. We are built and made for the community, by the community, in order to make minority students feel heard and listened to. MCFAB respects the interests of the Cornell student body and makes it its mission to bring diverse and exciting talents to campus.

name: Multicultural Greek and Fraternal Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, International/Multicultural, AY27 - Byline
description: The mission of our Council is to operate as a united governing body for all organizations. We are dedicated to promoting unity and serving as a support system for all organizations. We will serve as a model for the underrepresented student community and operate as a united body to effectively advocate the issues and concerns of our organizations and the entire campus community that we serve.

name: Native American and Indigenous Students At Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Student Groups for Student Services
description: Native American and Indigenous Students at Cornell (NAISAC) exists to promote and preserve understanding of Indigenous cultures of the Americas, to raise awareness of Indigenous issues, and to foster networks among American Indians, Alaska Natives, Native Hawaiians, First Nations, and other Indigenous students and alumni of Cornell University.

name: Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: Cornell Naval ROTC, through a disciplined, resilient, and collaborative culture, forges servant leaders committed to excellence.

name: Nazaqat
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: We aim to convey the elegance and beauty in Kathak, a classical Indian dance form, through creative fusion choreographies on semi-classical or modern music. We hope to make choreographies that preserve grace and story-telling in the dance form yet creatively combine it with contemporary Indian and Western music and dance.

name: Nexus at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, Sustainability/Environmental
description: Our mission is to redefine the scope of impact that Cornell students can make. We aim to develop novel solutions that will be deployed by global organizations to create positive social change. Our members think like researchers, build like engineers, and execute like entrepreneurs.

name: NOMAS: Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: Cornell NOMAS is the Cornell University Student Chapter of the National Organization of Minority Architects (NOMA), a national organization founded in 1971 to support and advocate for the advancement of underrepresented professionals in architecture and the built environment. Since 1992, Cornell NOMAS has served as a critical platform for mentorship, academic excellence, professional development, and community engagement within the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. We are committed to promoting equity, representation, and culturally responsive design while preparing students to become leaders who shape a more just and inclusive profession.

name: Orchestra Board at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of the Cornell Orchestra Board is to unify the members of the Cornell Symphony Orchestra and Cornell Chamber Orchestra through various performance, service, and social events throughout the year. The board also plans orchestra tours and community outreach events in the Ithaca community.

name: Order of Omega
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The Mission of the Order of Omega, Beta Upsilon Chapter, is to bring together leaders from diverse backgrounds within the Cornell Greek system in promoting our identity as the Greek honors society. We will represent the positive attributes of the Greek community and advocate for chapter philanthropy events while discouraging and shunning the negative aspects of our community that prevent us from representing ourselves and our peers in a positive light.

name: Organization of Urban and Regional Studies
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: It is the mission of the Organization of Urban and Regional Studies (OURS) at Cornell University to effectively and responsibly facilitate and maintain four primary activities: Forming a community among the undergraduate students in the Urban & Regional Studies program in the College of Architecture, Art, and Planning. Giving students a wider perspective of the field of urban and regional studies through hands-on urban experience. Providing a voice for undergraduate students in City & Regional Planning Department affairs. Acting as a resource for students to connect students to alumni, internships, and jobs, so that students graduate from the URS program with the greatest chances for professional success. Amended on: April 26, 2014

name: Outdoor Odyssey
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience, Sustainability/Environmental, AY27 - Byline
description: Outdoor Odyssey is a completely student run organization designed to help incoming Cornell freshmen and transfer students adjust to a new college experience. The program offers a variety of outdoor preorientation programs, led by specially trained upperclassmen guides, each August. Odyssey strives to maintain inclusivity and welcomes participants of all levels of outdoor experience.

name: Panhellenic Association at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: SFL - Greek, Community Service
description: The official name of this organization is the Cornell Panhellenic Association, and the Panhellenic Council is the governing organization of the 12 Panhellenic sorority chapters at Cornell. The purpose of the Panhellenic Association shall be to develop and maintain women's fraternity life and interfraterity relations at a high level of accomplishment.

name: PATCH - Pre-Professional Association Toward Careers in Health
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: PATCH is an organization within the College of Human Ecology that strives to help pre-health students develop their abilities, potential, and passions as they explore human health careers and prepare for medical or graduate school. Through participating in community outreach activities, students can expect to develop leadership, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. PATCH brings together pre-health students in a supportive, educational atmosphere that fosters growth and development through intellectual conversations and faculty interaction, encourages health career exploration and diversity, and translates academic pursuits into community action and service.

name: Pi Alpha Xi
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The mission of this Honor Society is 1) to recognize high scholarship, 2) to foster good relationships among its members, 3) to promote or to facilitate the exchange of ideas among members of the professions, and 4) to establish cordial relations among students, educators and industry members.

name: Pre-Veterinary Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife
description: The Pre-Veterinary Society is organized to provide a support network and pre-professional network for pre-vet students at Cornell. This includes seminars, contacts for important faculty members, advising for classes and applications, and hosting events during the year for local causes.

name: Professional Fraternity Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of this council is to maintain the system of PFOs, connect the PFOs in their individual points of action, support the recruitment of new members to PFOs, build relationships and networks between its PFO members, support mutual efforts of fundraising by the PFOs, and provide professional opportunities to the members of the PFOs, general student body, and community at large.

name: Prospect of Whitby
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, International/Multicultural, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: The Prospect of Whitby has been a cooperative house at Cornell University since 1965. We are dedicated to social justice, inclusion, and creating a safe living space for people with diverse life experiences.

name: Quodlibet
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural
description: To provide a lively forum for all those interested in all things medieval on campus.  To organize a series of lectures to highlight current research topics relating to medieval studies.

name: Raptor Program at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife
description: It shall be the purpose of CRP to care for, rehabilitate, and manage a variety of captive raptor species. It shall train students in the proper care and handling of raptors. It shall engage the campus and greater community through formal and informal education programs designed to teach audiences about raptor biology and conservation. It shall select species for propagation and appropriately pair breeding individuals.

name: REACH - Raising Education Attainment Challenge
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: REACH is a service-learning organization that focuses on tutoring and mentoring students in and around Ithaca. We love volunteering and working with students to better their learning experiences.

name: Red Key Athlete Honor Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: To recognize outstanding undergraduate contributors to both Cornell athletics and the Cornell community. We value academic achievement, propagation of fellowship and strong loyalty amongst all Cornell athletes, and enhancement of the Cornell and Ithaca communities through service.

name: Redbud Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Sustainability/Environmental, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: Statement on the Cooperative Identity A cooperative is an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social, and cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly-owned and democratically- controlled enterprise. Cooperatives are based on the values of self-help, self-responsibility, democracy, equality, equity, and solidarity. In the tradition of their founders, co-operative members believe in the ethical values of honesty, openness, social responsibility, and caring for others.  The cooperative principles are guidelines by which co-operatives put their values into practice.

name: Residence Hall Association
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services
description: A.	Promote and foster a sense of cohesion within the campus residential community; B.	Provide training for residential community leaders in the areas of leadership, communication, representation, programming, advocacy, and personal and community development; C.	Involve its members as active participants in the process of self-governance; D.	Provide a forum in order to communicate and exchange ideas, as well as voice concerns about residential community life; E.	Provide programs and activities through which its members may have the opportunity to grow and develop emotionally, physically, academically, and socially; F.	Identify, investigate, and share information about areas of student concern relating to the residential community through cooperative interactions; and G.	Represent the interests and concerns of its members to University decision- makers, especially the Department of Residential and New Student Programs and the Department of Student and Campus Life.

name: Risley Ministry for Arts and Shops Development
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Visual Arts
description: Within Risley, The Shops have historically been student run, allowing all possible creativity and use. However, student safety is at risk without proper training and knowledge. Therefore, we have created The Risley Ministry of Arts and Shops to balance student safety and student use. The mission of the Risley Ministry for Arts and Shops Development (RMASD) is to promote safety throughout the shop spaces, promote communication among residents, student volunteer managers, residential staff, professional staff, and the public, and promote documentation with standard operating procedures, inventories, and minutes. The Ministry also seeks to progress and develop the Risley Shops into a functioning space for artists and performers of both Risley and the University as a whole.

name: Rocketry at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: The Cornell Rocketry Team designs, manufactures and tests a high-powered rocket every year for competition in the Spaceport America Cup. We travel to IREC in Midland, TX to compete against 150 other collegiate teams from 22 different countries. The primary goal at competition is to launch the rocket to exactly 10,000 feet using our Student Research and Developed (SRAD) hybrid rocket motor. Every year, our rocket carries with it a unique scientific payload that leverages the high altitude or high acceleration environment onboard the rocket. The team designs and manufactures almost every part of the rocket in house, making use of a variety of lab spaces on campus.

name: Sailing Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: A competitive sailboat racing team that competes throughout the Inter-collegiate sailing association (ICSA).

name: Scabbard & Blade Society
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Believing that military service is an obligation of citizenship, and that the greater opportunities afforded college men and women for the study of military science place upon them certain responsibilities as citizens, we cadet officers in various colleges and universities conferring baccalaureate degrees, do form this society and adopt this constitution in order to united in closer relationship the military departments of American universities and colleges; to preserve and develop the essential qualities of good and efficient officers; to prepare ourselves as educated men and women to take a more active part and to have greater influence in the military affairs of the communities in which we may reside; and above all to spread intelligent information concerning the military requirements of our country.

name: SensTech
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: SensTech is a biomedical engineering project team that gives students hands-on experience in biosensor research, engineering design, business development, outreach, and biomedical science. Each year, the team participates in the international SensUs competition, where university teams develop biosensors in response to a healthcare-focused competition theme. Through this work, members from a broad range of majors and schools collaborate to design, build, test, and present a biosensor prototype and business model. SensTech aims to prepare students with real-world experience in interdisciplinary product development while creating impactful sensor technologies that address unmet needs in human health.

name: Slope Day Programming Board
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts, Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The Slope Day Programming Board serves as an organization through which students work with faculty, staff, and other community members in all colleges, departments, and divisions to plan and promote Slope Day. The Board promotes a day that fosters a safe and healthy environment with multiple social and recreational options. The group recruits and trains students for Slope Day to assist with monitoring, entertainment, food and beverage distribution, and other activities. The group will be responsible for use of appropriated student funds, pursuant to guidelines established by the Student Assembly, and partake in the University's efforts through cooperation and coordination with its departments through the Slope Day Steering Committee. The Board works with the administration and the Student Assembly in the development of policy for the day.

name: Snodgrass and Wigglesworth - Cornell Undergraduate Entomology Club
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The purpose of Snodgrass and Wigglesworth shall be to, in affiliation with the Cornell Department of Entomology, promote the study and appreciation of arthropods. The goals of Snodgrass and Wigglesworth are: 1. To foster a cohesive community among the Cornell undergraduates interested in arthropods, with a focus on insects. 2. To spread awareness and appreciation of entomology throughout the Cornell campus and Ithaca area. 3. To be a resource for peer mentorship, informal outreach events, and education for the Cornell campus community and Ithaca area. 4. To locate and describe the larvae of Merope tuber.

name: Sociedad de Debate en EspaÃ±ol de Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Political/Speech/Debate
description: The Society of Spanish Debating is an organization which seeks to teach debating skills to Spanish speaking students at Cornell. Its mission is to promote the Spanish language in Cornell, and train and teach to analyze rhetoric, logic, and proper presentation of arguments and positions in Spanish in hopes of creating community leaders, lawyers, and politicians who will be able to connect, understand, and better represent the Spanish speaking communities of the United States. Furthermore the Society of Spanish Debating will host and compete in debate tournaments that will be in the Spanish language. It's vision is to spread Spanish debating throughout the United States helping to establish Spanish Debating Societies and Spanish Debating circuits with the ultimate goal of seeing a National Spanish Debate tournament come to fruition.

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Engineering
description: The Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE), Inc. is a non-profit organization dedicated to increasing the participation of Hispanic professionals and college students in the fields of engineering, technology, science, and math.

name: Society of Physics Students
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: To support, uplift, and advocate for the Cornell undergraduate physics community

name: Society of Women Engineers at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The Cornell Student Section of the Society of Women Engineers promotes women in Engineering by advocating the importance of diversity and by uniting resources to encourage academic, leadership, professional, and personal excellence for the entire Engineering community.

name: Solar Boat at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The purpose of CUSB is to provide a hands-on engineering experience to students of a wide array of majors, including engineering and business majors. CUSB will give these students the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to a real-world project to supplement their learning from the general curriculum.

name: South Asian Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: We, the members of the South Asian community at Cornell University, do hereby establish the South Asian Council to serve as the umbrella organization for all organizations at Cornell University that are concerned with South Asian identity, representation, and issues. The South Asian Council will aim to raise awareness and advocate for South Asian interests, provide support for the South Asian community, and build collaborations internal and external to the community.

name: Speech and Debate Society at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Political/Speech/Debate
description: The purpose of the Cornell Speech and Debate Society is to provide an opportunity for Cornell undergraduate students to compete in organized intercollegiate debate and speech competitions, as well as to conduct other activities associated with college forensics. The Cornell Speech and Debate Society is a registered student organization at Cornell University

name: State of the Pod
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Publication/Media, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: State of the Pod was founded on the mission to inform and engage the public on emerging issues in science and technology. The podcast production seeks to foster scientific inquiry for both its participants and broader Ithaca community while offering an accessible platform for all students to develop the skills necessary to produce and host original content on the SOTP podcast.

name: Steel Bridge at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team
description: The purpose of Steel Bridge is to apply and enrich knowledge gained in the classroom, to become acquainted and to practice working together effectively, to learn to overcome the various challenges associated with designing an engineered project, and to create a successful end project.

name: Student Activities Funding Commission
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The SAFC allocates funds to nearly 750 undergraduate student organizations. Our mission is to support undergraduate organizations in their ability to foster community and belonging at Cornell through funding opportunities.

name: Student Athlete Advisory Committee
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: To enhance the total student-athlete experience at Cornell by promoting opportunity, protecting student-athlete well-being, and fostering a positive student-athlete image.

name: Student Programming Council
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The Student Programming Council is an umbrella organization for our major programming organizations on campus. We elevate the student experience by creating memories for all students at Cornell.

name: Students Against the Sexual Solicitation of Youth
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Students Against the Sexual Solicitation of Youth (SASSY) was founded in 2007 through a Cornell Alternative Breaks trip since 2003, is committed to raising awareness and transforming public perception of the Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children (CSEC). SASSY works directly with Girls Educational and Mentoring Services (GEMS), a non-profit agency in New York City, whose mission is to "empower girls and young women, ages 12–24, who have experienced commercial sexual exploitation and domestic trafficking to exit the commercial sex industry and develop to their full potential. GEMS is committed to ending commercial sexual exploitation and domestic trafficking by changing individual lives, transforming public perception, and revolutionizing the systems and policies that impact commercially sexually exploited youth." SASSY has engaged with the Cornell community while maintaining and strengthening its relationship with and support for GEMS. SASSY has hosted several workshops, discussions, and movie screenings for the Cornell community.

name: Students for Early College Access
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Students for Early College Access (SECA) aims to combat educational inequities by empowering under-resourced and underserved students—particularly in the Ithaca and Tompkins County area—with the tools, knowledge, and support needed to pursue higher education. Through partnerships with local schools and other student organizations at Cornell, we provide interactive college-readiness programming, academic resources, and mentorship to guide students through the college application process. Our mission is to expand access, raise awareness, and foster equity by equipping students with the agency to make informed choices about their educational futures.

name: Sustainable Design at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: Cornell University Sustainable Design promotes education through action, empowerment, and innovation with several design-build projects. We utilize an interdisciplinary, research-based approach to create resilient structures in the built environment and realize a future of ecological, social, and economic sustainability.

name: The Wildlife Society Student Chapter at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Animals/Wildlife, Sustainability/Environmental
description: The objective of this organization is to promote students' awareness of wildlife ecology and conservation.

name: Translator Interpreter Program
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The Translator Interpreter Program (TIP) at the Cornell Language Resource Center trains bilingual and multilingual Cornell students to serve as volunteer translators/interpreters for community agencies in emergency and non-emergency situations.

name: Triphammer Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: Triphammer Cooperative is one of the university's cooperative residences, a collaborative and independent community governed by its student residents.

name: TST BOCES Career Skills at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Career Skills is a career exploration program at Cornell University designed to teach vocational-related skills to students who have an IEP (individual educational plan). These are students working towards acquiring a CDOS (Career Development Occupational Studies) Commencement Credential or the SACC. Collaborating with the Einhorn Center for Community Engagement, Career Skills provides student exploration of a variety of realistic career options on the Cornell campus. Cornell student mentors ("peer buddies") will partner with TST BOCES students and staff to help facilitate this process.

name: Undergraduate Biomedical Engineering Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The BMES Undergraduate Chapter aims to support undergraduate biomedical engineering students in their social and academic development at Cornell, as well as to provide support through research and employment resources. We also aim to educate the Cornell and Ithaca community on the field of biomedical engineering, and to provide information about the field and major to students not affiliated with Cornell's undergraduate biomedical engineering program.

name: Undergraduate Historical Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, Publication/Media
description: The Cornell Undergraduate Historical Society builds a community within the undergraduate student body that appreciates and strives to learn more of historical topics and methodology, as well as seeks to share this love of history with the general community. This is accomplished through several activities: publishing a journal ("Ezra's Archives"), running the History Advising Program, bringing speakers to campus, and holding many various academic and social events for the club itself.

name: Undergraduate Mathematics Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: We are dedicated to making mathematics accessible and fun to all Cornell students, as well as to enhancing the experience of undergraduate math study.

name: Undergraduates in Linguistics at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Education/Human Services, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The Undergraduates in Linguistics at Cornell is the undergraduate student group of the Cornell Department of Linguistics. It serves to provide opportunities for linguistics majors, minors, and other interested students to convene, learn more about the field, and promote linguistics at the undergraduate level in the Cornell community and the broader academic community.

name: Underrepresented Minorities in Computing
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Engineering
description: The mission of Underrepresented Minorities in Computing is to foster an environment that empowers underrepresented minorities in the computing fields through career development, community building and academic support.

name: United Way Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The mission of Cornell United Way is to boost education, promote socioeconomic mobility, and increase access to health resources in and around Tompkins County.

name: Unmanned Air Systems, (CUAir)
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: Project Team, PROF: Engineering
description: Designing, building, and flying a custom unmanned aerial system to educate, innovate, and ignite passion in our members.

name: Wait Terrace Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, Health/Wellbeing, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: To facilitate learning and community in a residential context.

name: Wanawake Wa Wari Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, International/Multicultural, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: Wanawake Wa Wari was originally founded in 1968 by a group of Black women who felt the need for an atmosphere that promoted self-awareness and personal confidence.  Since that time Wari has served as a place where women of African descent have prepared for the world academically, culturally, and socially.  It has also provided an atmosphere where women feel comfortable to deal with the issues that relate to their lives and history in the Ithaca community and beyond.  We are striving to continue this tradition.

name: Watermargin Cooperative
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - AFFILIATION: HRL/WCHS - Residential, International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: HRL Co-Ops
description: Watermargin was founded in 1947 by a group of World War II veterans who shared the purpose of promoting understanding between people of different races and religious affiliations. Over the years, the focus has expanded to encompass all intergroup relations. In the 1960's, Watermargin went co-ed, leading to a change in the motto from "All Men are Brothers" to "All People are Family." Watermargin's evolving mission is to encourage the expression of diverse views, to struggle against injustice, and to build communities. (http://www.watermargin.org/a/index.html)

name: Willard Straight Hall Student Union Board (SUB)
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AY27 - Byline
description: The Student Union Board aims to celebrate Willard Straight Hall's historical responsibility and Cornell's student culture by hosting events that build social relationships within the Cornell community, welcoming all students back to at the start of the Fall and Spring semester through fun and unique activities, and supporting and recognizing the cultural and social diversity of the student community throughout the school year.

name: Wind Ensembles at Cornell University
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of CU Winds is to build, maintain and support a wind band and chamber winds community on the Cornell campus and in the surrounding Ithaca area. It gives Cornell students with musical experience the opportunity to rehearse and perform with a larger ensemble. Additionally, CU Winds promotes the appreciation of wind band music through concert performances, new music commissions, workshops, etc.

name: Women in Computing at Cornell
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Women in Computing at Cornell strives to make computing inclusive for all. We aim to foster a supportive community of women* and allies equipped with the resources needed to recognize and overcome challenges. By creating opportunities for technical and leadership growth, we work to ensure that people of all identities are able to discover and pursue their interests and talents in order to positively impact the future of tech. *All gender identities are welcome and supported!

name: Women Leadership in Hospitality (WLiH)
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - PROF: Business and Management, AFFILIATION: Nolan Hotel School
description: Women Leadership in Hospitality is an organization dedicated to providing education, resources, mentorship, and leadership opportunities to women in order to empower them to be successful leaders in the world of hospitality and business.

name: Youth Outreach Undergraduates Reshaping Success
category: Undergrad University Student Organization (USO) - Community Service
description: Y.O.U.R.S. aims to provide opportunities for children aged 7 to 17 living in mobile home parks near Ithaca.  Y.O.U.R.S. volunteers work with the children who attend our program to develop healthy life-skills, self-esteem, leadership skills, and individual goals.  Each volunteer attends at least one of three weekly programs: Monday Makers, Tech Tuesday, Wellness Wednesday, or Thursday for the Earth. On Mondays, volunteers emphasize hands-on activities; they work one-on-one with the children to create a craft or science project that they can take home. On Tuesdays, volunteers work with youth on an ongoing science project presented to the group at the end of the semester. On Wednesdays, volunteers engage in fun, health-focused activities with the children, such as cooking, arts and crafts, and fitness programs. On Thursdays, volunteers work with youth to build awareness of environmental issues and implement skills for conservation.

name: A BIRDSONG Program
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: Building inclusive research and designing supportive outreach and networking for growing talents Outreach programs in STEM provide powerful opportunities for learning. For kids, these programs can cultivate life-long interests in STEM topics and even ignite the pursuit of STEM- related careers. However, communication and perceptual differences/disabilities make accessing community spaces and outreach materials inaccessible for many people. Furthermore, institutional opportunities to train STEM students in disability justice, accessibility and inclusive practices are rare. This team’s goal is to bring Cornell STEM students, TST BOCES students and the Lab of Ornithology together to enhance their ability to communicate STEM-related content and improve the impact of outreach programs. Leveraging a shared interest in birds, the team is building lasting relationships across the community to support these goals.

name: 23 New Org
category: Department
description: This is a placeholder for new org registration to be able to attend Workshops.

name: Advocacy Center of Tompkins County
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: Supporting survivors of sexual and domestic violence

name: Alumni Affairs & Development
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: As a Cornell student, you’re now part of a life-long network of Cornellians that spans time zones, generations, disciplines, and life experiences. Today’s graduates join a community of more than 250,000 alumni who live and work in communities around the globe. We invite you to connect with the amazing professional and social network of Cornell alumni. Join regional events happening in your area when you’re home on break. Connect with alumni online. Or get involved in the Senior Class Campaign. After you graduate, check out your local Cornell Club and connect with Cornellians here, there, and everywhere!

name: American Indian and Indigenous Studies Program
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: As Cornell University's American Indian and Indigenous Studies Program (AIISP), our mission is to aid the development of new generations of educated Indigenous and non-Indigenous people who will contemplate, study and contribute to the building of Indigenous nations and communities on a global scale.

name: American Red Cross (Community Partner)
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: Red Cross volunteers and staff work to deliver vital services – from providing relief and support to those in crisis, to helping you be prepared to respond in emergencies.

name: Anatomic Pathology Faculty
category: Department

name: Asian & Asian American Center
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental, International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Founded in 2009, the Asian & Asian American Center (A3C) brings together the rich diversity of Asian Pacific Islander Desi American experiences (to include East, South, Southeast Asian, Pacific Islander, bi/multi-racial/ethnic, etc.) to foster an inclusive Cornell campus community. Our programs focus on advocacy, education, identity and community building.

category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental, Health/Wellbeing
description: Cornell Outdoor Education develops teamwork, leadership, and growth through outdoor experience. We do so by: Teaching outdoor skills and judgment for lifelong recreation and fitness. Igniting a passion for experiential learning. Enhancing initiative, self-reliance, and compassion for others. Cornell Outdoor Education serves the broad membership of the Cornell community: students and student instructors, faculty and staff, alumni and friends, local community and outside groups. We enhance academic performance and success in the workplace by developing leadership, teamwork and personal achievement through experience-based education in the outdoor environment at Cornell University and around the world. Cornell Outdoor Education programs place participants into hands-on learning situations that promote honest and constructive assessment of individual and group performance, provide natural and immediate consequences to actions, and promote personal growth. Our programs encourage participants to gain a sense of perspective in their own lives, and build support networks that develop meaningful lifelong friendships. Finally, we include fun with learning. By integrating these experiences into the rich academic curriculum and physical setting of our University, Cornell Outdoor Education plays a unique and vitally important role in developing the Leaders of the 21st Century.
