name: German Studies
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: German Studies at Cornell enables students to develop the linguistic, literary, and cultural competency required of world citizens in the twenty-first century.  The interdisciplinary and cross-cultural orientation of our curriculum is designed to fulfill the needs of our diverse student population.  We encourage students to choose from the broad range of courses we offer in collaboration with other units such as Government, Philosophy, History, Comparative Literature, Jewish Studies, and Performing and Media Arts. Our curriculum is inspired by three core tenets: The literary and visual arts are unique realms of thought and experimentation that constitute a source of knowledge in its own right. Engagement with the distinct ways these domains have been investigated in the German intellectual tradition provides a crucial basis for critical reflection on society and culture. The greatest insights that teachers and students produce arise in a dynamic environment that fosters cooperative learning, the pleasure of discovery, and rigorous intellectual mentoring. Our courses emphasize close analysis of texts and artifacts, as sustained at all times by thoughtful reflection on the concepts that guide our investigations.  We regard essay writing in both English and German as central to our core mission of teaching students to think critically and develop cogent, rhetorically effective arguments.  Our curriculum closely integrates the study of language and culture at all levels of instruction.  We regularly offer seminars on such topics as modern literature and aesthetics; space and architecture in fictional worlds; avant-garde movements and artistic perception; contemporary literature, globalization and migration; critical theory; the detective novel; politics and history on stage; homo oeconomicus; Marx, Nietzsche, Freud; political theory and cinema; psychoanalysis; web culture. We warmly welcome and encourage students to pursue German Studies as a vibrant part of their general education, whether as a major or minor; as a double major alongside another discipline; in preparation for graduate school; or as a stepping stone to an international professional career.  Our diverse course offerings fall in the broader themes of: Culture and Society, Literature and Philosophy, Aesthetics and Media, and Critical and Political Thought.  Therefore, we seek to engage our students' intellect and imagination by valorizing the plurality of intellectual impulses that comprise our field and relating them purposefully to each student's academic goals.

description: The Cornell University Graduate and Professional Student Assembly serves as an official voice for the the nearly 7,000 graduate and professional students at Cornell. In addition to representing the students in matters of university governance, the GPSA has the responsibility for setting and administering the Student Activity Fee for graduate and professional students. The GPSA is a valuable component of graduate or professional education for those who hope to be affiliated with a university in the future. The GPSA regularly meets with the President and Provost, and it sends representatives to the Employee Assembly, the undergraduate Student Assembly, and the Faculty Senate. Involvement in the GPSA can provide valuable experience in the mechanics of shared governance in a university setting. Every graduate and professional student at Cornell can have a voice in the GPSA, and we're working to encourage each other to speak up to make sure everybody is heard! Each graduate or professional field can send a representative to the GPSA – current representatives and vacancies are listed on the Assembly website – and any graduate student can serve on a GPSA committee.

name: Hunter R. Rawlings III Cornell Presidential Research Scholars
category: Department
description: The Hunter R. Rawlings III Cornell Presidential Research Scholars (RCPRS) Program provides highly motivated undergraduate students with the opportunity to engage in sustained, faculty-mentored research throughout their undergraduate careers. Open to students from all Cornell colleges and across every discipline—including the humanities, social sciences, physical and biological sciences, engineering, and the arts—the program supports students in pursuing their intellectual interests through original research in close collaboration with faculty and other mentors. Each year, the program supports up to 200 students. The majority are selected as incoming first-year students, with up to 25 additional scholars admitted annually as rising juniors. The RCPRS program was established in 1996 through an anonymous gift to Cornell University. In 2006, Cornell's Board of Trustees renamed the program in honor of former university president Hunter R. Rawlings III, recognizing his enduring commitment to students, scholarship, and undergraduate research.

We cultivate academic excellence while fostering a collaborative community where scholars support one another, engage with curiosity and purpose, and develop a lifelong commitment to giving back. Through mentorship, resources, and shared experiences, we prepare our scholars to lead with integrity, serve their communities, and create lasting positive impact in the world.

name: Laidlaw Leadership and Research Program
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental

Eligibility First- and second-year students from any college or major may apply. You should have a strong academic background and must be able to commit to full participation in the program. U.S. citizenship is not required. In order to be eligible for program funding, scholars must commit to all components of the program. Upon acceptance, scholars will be required to sign a commitment form. These expectations and important upcoming dates are outlined below. If you have any questions about what full commitment to the program entails, please contact us at laidlaw.scholars@cornell.edu

name: Language Resource Center
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: The Language Resource Center (LRC) is a hub for language innovation and collaboration at Cornell University. Our mission is to connect, support, and empower language learners and teachers. The LRC provides flexible physical and virtual spaces, facilitates access to resources, and advocates best practices. Our vision is to raise awareness of the value of language learning, leverage technology in service of cultural and social experiences, and grow the language community within and beyond Cornell.

name: Latina/o Studies Program & LSP Student Success Office
category: Department - AFFILIATION: Departmental
description: Latina/o Studies is dedicated to the study of the historical, linguistic, literary, social, economic, and political experiences of a vastly heterogeneous population in the United States, that today totals over 55 million people.  Officially founded in 1987 as the Hispanic American Studies Program, our name was changed to the Latina/o Studies Program in 1995.  We nurture familia, inquire into the important questions of the day, and through our courses and other intellectual activities—conferences, lectures, exhibits, dialogues, and other research initiatives and activities--learn how Latinas/os contribute to a greater understanding of the world, through the analysis of politics, migration histories, health, labor insertion, literature, and the arts.

name: Latinx Student Empowerment

As a senior staff member of the Centers for Student Equity, Empowerment, and Belonging in the Dean of Student office, the Associate Dean of Students and Director of Latinx Student Empowerment leads strategic planning and collaborative partnerships to improve the Latinx/e student experience at Cornell University. They offer guidance to student organizations, coordinate and implement programming, and serve as a support network for Latinx/e students. A key priority is to design and implement student-centered initiatives that foster identity development, leadership skills, and a strong sense of belonging.

If you are interested in supporting our efforts or wish to join our diverse multicultural student organizations please contact us at msle@cornell.edu and we can help you get connected.

Our office in Washington, DC, is available for use by Cornell University faculty and staff conducting university business in the nation’s capital. Our staff offers support to Cornell representatives who travel to Washington to meet and communicate with members of Congress and other federal officials.

A fundamental mission of the OA is to engage constituencies across campus and increase participation in the shared governance process and voice effectively the interests and concerns of the non-academic members of the campus community. The OA serves to maintain channels and processes for the members' continuous involvement in the decision-making process of the University, and proactive improvement to the quality of life on campus. The OA also provides a method for synthesizing different opinions, concerns and ideas and a means of communicating them to the Administration, which supports and works closely with the Assemblies and their committees throughout the decision-making process.

description: If you want to be the best, learn with the best. At the Cornell Peter and Stephanie Nolan School of Hotel Administration, we've been pioneering, reimagining, and perfecting hospitality education for a century. We push boundaries in the pursuit of excellence and define the future of our industry. Our AACSB-accredited degree immerses you in a business education infused with the foundational knowledge of hospitality, services, and real estate. The Cornell Nolan School experience combines world-class classroom instruction with hands-on experiential learning and is the only Ivy League program of its kind. You'll join the ranks of our proud Hotelie community, which includes foremost leaders, innovators, and entrepreneurs in one of the most exciting industries around the globe.

We offer personalized service, event space and menus that include room rental cost, linens, LED candles, and a dance floor. This means working with those impacted by incarceration, governmental policy makers, researchers, nonprofit organizations, and community members to make structural changes: create safe and affordable housing, improve employment prospects, increase transportation access, close gaps in health care and other social services. Support Research Projects Become a part of the Friendship network that support people coming home from jail or prison Support administrative needs, attending zoom meeting and taking notes, emailing constituents with updates and help coordinate various activities

This area promotes awareness, identity exploration, community engagement, and self-advocacy. The office also facilitates educational resources and collaborates with community partners to help support undocumented and DACA students at Cornell. name: 14Strings! Cornell Filipino Rondalla
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Performing Arts
description: 14Strings! is a Filipino style Rondalla based in Ithaca, New York. The main instruments are 14 stringed plucked instruments like the bandurria, the laud (lute), and the octavina. Our mission is to further the appreciation for and engagement in the tradition of the Rondalla, both for our members and the wider Cornell and Ithaca communities. All are always welcome regardless of background or musical experience.

name: 180 Degrees Consulting at Cornell University
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management

Our team of passionate social impact leaders will develop professional skills through hands-on learning to solve modern business challenges.

name: A Seat at the Table
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: It is our purpose to provide a professional, supportive, educational, and social venue where all students can discuss issues affecting and pertaining to their respective communities as well as social issues which they feel passionate about, all through a business lens (i.e. freedom of speech and religion, race relations in the workplace, ESG and sustainability efforts, and more). Essentially, our priority is to allow for conversation and education surrounding Business Ethics and Human Resources in a way that develops students professionally through consulting projects.

name: AAP - Cornell AAP ASSOCIATION
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media, Visual Arts, AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: An anthology of projects from artists, architects, and planners, ASSOCIATION strives to highlight cross-disciplinary connections and reveal new relationships between the works produced by the three departments we represent. Through the careful curation and presentation of yearly submissions since 2005, each volume serves as a record of the work produced by the current AAP community, as well as a source of inspiration for years to come.

name: Absolute A Cappella
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Performing Arts
description: Established in 2001, Absolute A Cappella is an a cappella group at Cornell University and was founded on the core values of singing, friendship, and pineapples. Absolute performs two concerts each year as well as a variety of arch-sings. The group sings a range of genres, from indie pop to alt rock. Absolute is always finding exciting new ways to sing and perform, and most importantly, have fun while doing what we love.

name: Absolute Zero Break Dance Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Performing Arts
description: Our goals are the mastery of our bodies in dance through practice, and the fostering of relationships with crew members, breakdance club members, alumni, other dance troupes, the larger Cornell community, friends, and acquaintances through our love of breaking, funkstyles, and music.

name: Accentia Magazine
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media, Visual Arts
description: Accentia is a multilingual creative collective centered on displaying poetry, prose, and various creative writing mediums in non-English languages. We strive to accentuate the voices of creatives who speak a diverse array of languages and provide a space for open expression. Through our vast linguistic perspectives, we offer the opportunity for multilingual people, from native speakers to beginners, to tap into their artistic side.

name: ACE: The Ace/Asexual Support Group at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: ACE is a student-run social support group for individuals of the Cornell community who identify as ace/aro or ace/aro-questioning. ACE provides its members with a support network and a safe space to meet and discuss ace related issues and experiences. ACE is also dedicated to developing the ace community at Cornell and improving visibility and availability of information surrounding the ace community.

name: Adventist Christian Fellowship at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: We exist as a supportive ministry to students who desire to be part of an open and accepting Christian student organization. Our purpose is to know and experience the love that God has for us, to share in God's love for one another, and to live God's love before others. We're here to support each other in fellowship as well as to provide encouragement to the general community. We maintain active ties with the Ithaca Seventh-Day Adventist Church.

name: African Dance Repertoire
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Performing Arts
description: To foster the awareness of African cultures through music, dance, and theatrical performances both on and off campus.

name: AFROTC Detachment 520
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The mission of the Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC) 520th Cadet Wing is to recruit, educate, and develop cadets in a high-quality training environment and commission the strongest leaders for the United States Air Force and Space Force.

name: Aikido Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The Cornell Aikido Club promotes the study of the Japanese martial art, Aikido. We offer classes, resources on learning more about Aikido, and information on upcoming seminars.

name: Albanian Student Association at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The Albanian Student Association at Cornell brings together students of Albanian descent and everyone who wants to learn about Albanian history, culture, politics, and beyond. Our purpose is to provide an opportunity for Albanian students to meet, interact with each other, and help new students coming from Albania. ASAC serves to promote the awareness of cultural diversity on campus by organizing cultural and social events on campus. The membership of ASAC is open to all Albanian students and every student of Cornell University.

name: Alexander Hamilton Society
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Political/Speech/Debate
description: The Alexander Hamilton Society (AHS) is an independent, non-partisan, not-for-profit organization dedicated to promoting constructive debate on basic principles and contemporary issues in foreign, economic, and national security policy. AHS seeks to identify, educate, and launch young men and women into foreign policy and national security careers imbued with the Hamiltonian perspective of strong and principled American leadership in global affairs. Hamiltonians are united by a deep conviction, rooted in the history of the last century, that the world is a better, safer, and more prosperous place when the United States is willing and able to lead.

name: Alpha Epsilon Delta; Pre-Health Honor Society
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Alpha Epsilon Delta meetings provide a non-stressful environment for members to come together in a supportive setting to discuss and understand the full meaning of our pursuit of a career in healthcare. We discuss current medical events and ethical issues, host guest panels, share advice on the medical school application process, get certified in Narcan and CPR administration, and plan social and service events.

name: Alpha Iota Gamma Gamma Chapter
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Alpha Iota Gamma (╬æ I ╬ô) serves as a professional, academic, and social foundation for men and women dedicated to pursuing a career in healthcare. The brothers and sisters of Alpha Iota Gamma uphold a commitment to discipline, compassion, and integrity, key ethical pillars in healthcare and life. The bonds formed in Alpha Iota Gamma between students with diverse healthcare interests creates a comprehensive network at the undergraduate level and beyond. Members of Alpha Iota Gamma have the opportunity to meet other students interested in healthcare careers, get peer and professional level advice from other members and invited speakers, be involved in philanthropy and social events, and most importantly make friendships that will last years after graduating from Cornell.

name: Alpha Omega Epsilon Professional Engineering Sorority
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering
description: Our purpose is to promote ideals and objectives that further the advancement of female engineers and technical scientists and build a foundation for lifelong bonds of sisterhood.

name: Alpha Phi Omega - Gamma Chapter
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: Alpha Phi Omega is a national gender inclusive community service fraternity for college students. APO strives to help each member develop leadership skills, secure lasting friendships, and provide service to others. The award-winning Gamma Chapter has grown to into a close-knit organization of over 400 members, providing meaningful service to the Cornell campus, Ithaca community, and national and global organizations.

name: Alpha Zeta
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC)
description: Founded in 1901, the Cornell Chapter of Alpha Zeta is a co-ed, honors, professional, and social fraternity for anyone with an interest in agriculture. We provide a unique community on campus that provides opportunities for community service, social activities, and professional networking. The goals of our Fraternity are to foster high standards of scholarship, character, leadership, and fellowship and also to promote the advancement of agriculture. Our main agricultural outreach event, Ag Day, is held every semester and brings farm animals and agricultural equipment to the Ag Quad to expose the Cornell community to and educate them about agriculture. We also hold a number of philanthropy events every year which contribute to a handful of organizations including the 4-H Foundation, the American Red Cross, Heifer International, Adopt-a-Highway, and the Special Olympics.

name: Alpine Ski Racing
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: The Cornell Alpine Ski Team is a club sport open to all current undergraduate students at Cornell University. The team provides a format for competitive ski racing as well as development of new racers. We train on-snow at Greek Peak, which is conveniently located about 30 mins from campus.

name: Already Friendz at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: Already Friendz is a student-led mentorship program at Cornell that connects incoming transfer students with current Cornellians who have successfully navigated the transfer experience. Our mission is to ease the transition into Cornell by offering advice, guidance, and genuine friendship. We aim to ensure that every transfer student arrives feeling informed, prepared, and connected. At Cornell, you don’t have to start over—because through this community, we’re Already Friendz.

name: American Cancer Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: Our organization runs various events throughout the year to spread cancer awareness and raise money for the American Cancer Society.  Our biggest event is Relay for Life, an all-night fundraiser that the entire Cornell community is encouraged to attend.  We fundraise before and during the event, which includes speakers, performances, food, and activities.

name: American Fisheries Society Student Subunit at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Sustainability/Environmental
description: To advance the knowledge of fisheries and aquatic science at Cornell, promote professional development of undergraduate students, and facilitate collaboration of students and fisheries professionals at Cornell.

name: American India Foundation Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The purpose of the AIF Cornell Chapter shall be to provide an avenue for high-achieving undergraduate and graduate students with a passion for international development and social change to help create a more equitable India through ambassadorship and fundraising efforts supporting AIF’s initiatives in education, livelihood, and public health–improving the lives of India’s underprivileged.

name: American Institute of Architecture Students Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services, Visual Arts, AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: The AIAS Cornell Chapter aims to promote excellence in architectural education, training, and practice; to foster an appreciation of architecture and related disciplines; to enrich communities in a spirit of collaboration; and to organize undergraduate and graduate Cornell students and combine their efforts to advance the art and science of architecture.

name: American Lung Cancer Screening Initiative at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: ALCSIC aims to promote awareness for lung cancer screening for individuals at high-risk of developing lung cancer at Cornell University and the larger Ithaca community through educational efforts, community outreach, and health literacy engagement. Activities may include advocating for Congress members to support lung cancer bills, presenting to various stakeholders to build awareness, and working with local health departments to educate and bring actionable change to the community.

name: American Red Cross at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing
description: The American Red Cross prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors. The organization works closely with the American Red Cross to help fulfill its humanitarian missions and uphold its values.

name: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Cornell Chapter
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The purpose of the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Cornell Chapter is to cultivate a community of scholars dedicated to scientific discovery and promoting interdisciplinary research while giving students more opportunities to learn about the fields of biochemistry and molecular biology.

name: Anabel's Collaboration and Education
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Food/Drink
description: Passionate about food? Want to promote food justice on campus? For students interested in collaborating with Anabel's Grocery, our student-run nonprofit grocery store, join Anabel's Collaboration and Education. Help us develop projects that support a socially just and environmentally sound food system with an awesome team!

name: Animal Advocacy at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Animals/Wildlife
description: The purpose of Animal Advocacy at Cornell (AAC) shall be to provide a space for individuals of all backgrounds who have an interest in ending suffering and exploitation of all animals, through advocacy, education, outreach, campaigning, and a plant-based lifestyle. AAC seeks to increase the accessibility of a plant-based diet and help individuals explore the world of plant-based eating.

name: Anjali at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Performing Arts
description: Founded in 2011, Cornell Anjali aims to spread awareness of South Asian classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, and Odissi. We perform as a group both on and off campus, sponsor many South Asian cultural events, perform at our annual showcase, and also hold workshops for those interested in the aforementioned art forms. We aim to  perform, promote, and spread the love of South Asian classical dance throughout Cornell.

name: Applied Public Policy Strategies at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Political/Speech/Debate
description: With the ever-evolving policy and governance sphere, Applied Public Policy Strategies (APPS) empowers students to deliver innovative, data-driven solutions to complex government and policy challenges. By combining strategic consulting skills with a passion for public service, we foster impactful change and develop the next generation of civic-minded leaders at Cornell and beyond. Working with leading think tanks, non-profits, governments, and industry innovators, we strive to drive meaningful policy outcomes and create sustainable solutions that address today’s most pressing challenges.

name: Arab Student Association
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of ASA is to create a welcoming and inclusive community for individuals interested in Arab language, culture, and heritage, with the goal of fostering cross-cultural dialogue and mutual understanding on campus and beyond. Those individuals also have the opportunity to increase awareness of pertinent issues in the Arab world both on the Cornell campus and in the larger Ithaca community. ASA is a nonpartisan student group. As such, it will not be associated with or have any bias towards regional Arab political, religious, and ideological entities.

name: Archery Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The Cornell Archery Club provides a forum for the discussion and practice of the traditional sport of archery.  Our charge is to promote an environment where any and all members of the Cornell community can participate in a classic sport and learn the elements of collegiate archery. In pursuit of this goal, we facilitate weekly shoots, where archers of all skill levels can practice and socialize, learning from more experienced archers and developing their own skills and their understanding of the sport. We also attend local, state and national competitions for members who are interested in competing.

name: Architects, Artists, and Planners of Color
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: The mission and purpose of Architects, Artists, and Planners of Color shall be to amplify the BIPOC voices in AAP. AAPOC does this by creating a safe and welcoming space that fosters inclusion and a sense of unity throughout AAP. AAPOC works to create a network that supports BIPOC students.

name: Armenian Student Organization
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: To foster community among students and locals with an interest in Armenian heritage on Cornell's campus through social/cultural events, Armenian language and culture classes, and educational events (guest speakers, workshops, conferences). To educate the Cornell campus about the Armenian language, culture, and history. To establish a greater and more inclusive sense of community by collaborating with other organizations.

name: Art and Business Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Publication/Media
description: The Art and Business Club at Cornell (ABCC) helps Cornell artists to build a clearer public identity: who they are, what they make, and why their work matters. ABCC turns artwork into profiles, exhibitions, social storytelling, and eventually stronger connections to galleries and collectors. We aim to give student artists the polish and platform they deserve, showcase their work to wider audiences, and help them enter the professional art world. We welcome students from every background who are interested in the intersection of art and business.

name: Artistic Beads Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Visual Arts
description: The purpose of the Artistic Beads Club shall be to teach its members to make a variety of objects out of beads and bond with peers in a safe space.

name: Asha Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Community Service
description: Asha Cornell works to bring social awareness about the plight of education into the Cornell community through events such as fundraisers and other cultural activities. These activities include celebrations of Indian culture such as classical concerts featuring renowned Indian artists and movie series of recent Bollywood films, through which we hope the Cornell community attains a deeper glimpse into Indian culture. The funds we collect go towards catalyzing socio-economic change in India through the education of underprivileged children.

name: Asian American Intervarsity
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: Asian American InterVarsity is a group of students on campus with a vision to see students transformed, campuses renewed, and world changers developed. Through sharing the wide range of stories that make up the Asian American experience and exploring how they have shaped us, AAIV exists to explore how Jesus can transform pain and brokeness into celebration and restoration for Asian Americans.

name: Asian Pacific Americans for Action
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: APAA (established in 1972) is a group of passionate students dedicated to advocating for the AAPI community at Cornell. APAA builds on its past work in promoting the fundamental importance of political education and history through advocacy and discussion. AAPA is committed to furthering AAPI awareness on campus and to politically empowering and advocating for the needs of Asian-Pacific American students. Furthermore, APAA builds coalitions with other students of color and social justice groups to facilitate a more unified community of color. In the past two years, APAA held discussions on revolutionaries and thinkers like Grace Lee Boggs as well as relevant issues in the AAPI community such as affirmative action, rising gun violence in the AAPI community, and Asian-American history. We are also engaging with the greater Cornell community through fundraisers, panels, and other events to raise awareness about AAPI issues. APAA also publishes a literary magazine called Parallax, an Asian American social and political journal that highlights historical and contemporary AAPI topics of interest.

name: Asociación de CentroAmericanos Unidos
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of ACaU is to provide a secondary home for Central American students and anyone interested in Central American culture. Thus, ACaU fundamentally prioritizes empowering Central American students while fostering awareness of its rich, complex culture at Cornell University and the greater Ithaca area.

name: Asociación de Sudamericanos Unidos
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: The purpose of ASaU is to increase South American visibility within the greater Ithaca area, mainly serving Cornell University students. ASaU aims to foster a community for this underrepresented community while welcoming others as a learning opportunity.

name: Assisting People Across Nations
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The purpose of APAN is to provide a platform for students to engage in humanitarian fundraising efforts that support global human rights initiatives. Our focus is on raising awareness and financial resources for nonprofits that provide medical aid and essential services in crisis-affected regions. By supporting a range of organizations rather than one individual organization, we empower members to design and lead targeted fundraising campaigns aligned with causes they are passionate about, fostering leadership development and a strong sense of global responsibility.

name: Association of Latino Professionals For America
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: ALPFA’s mission is to develop and inspire future leaders by providing leadership and professional development opportunities and fostering a collaborative community of exceptional leaders. Our Cornell chapter strives to create a community and collaborative, excellent leaders. To empower and develop leaders of character for the nation in every sector of the global economy.

name: Assorted Aces
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: Established in 2016, The Assorted Aces is Cornell's first premiere dance troupe with a focus on molding absolute beginners into skilled dancers. When welcoming dancers, no dance experience is necessary; in fact, we prioritize students who are completely new to dancing. For our experienced dancers, we tailor to their needs by developing their technique, choreography, and leadership skills. Our mission is to offer the opportunity to both inexperienced and trained dancers to grow and develop in a supportive dance community. Even though we are only 10 years old, our group has already surpassed 100 dancers… and we are always looking for more!

name: Automotive Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive, Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: We aim to provide a platform for students to share and enjoy a common interest, passion, and hobby: Cars. We welcome all enthusiasts on campus for social events, car shows, discussions, and collaborations with other nearby car clubs. We aim to create a community of students passionate about cars and any motorsport.

name: AXSigma - Alpha Chi Sigma
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Our organization seeks to bring together people interested in chemistry, both to advance the science of chemistry and to advance the goals of those interested in the field. We reach out to youth organizations to try to raise interest in chemistry, and we connect our members to a diverse network of alumni whose goals and interests align with those of our current members.

name: Badminton at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: Badminton Cornell is a competitive group of badminton players training to improve at all skill levels through several weekly practices.  We also travel to several tournaments every year in the upstate New York area with all levels of players.

name: Ballet and Books
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service
description: We are a community based organization dedicated to strengthening the confidence and community of young children through dance while building literacy skills and excitement for reading. We pride ourselves on serving a diverse community of families and coming from diverse backgrounds ourselves.

name: Bangladeshi Students Association

name: Banking Club At Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management

category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Performing Arts

This purpose shall be fulfilled through the medium of Black Gospel music. The Ensemble shall carry out its suited by performing at various campus programs and community activities.

name: Barbell Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive

category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of the organization will be to encompass various forms of dance in a relaxed and fun environment, to encourage members to maximize their dance and performing potential by utilizing all BASE has to offer, and to create a opportunity for members to form close friendships through a mutual love for dance.

name: Baseball Club at Cornell University
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive

As part of the Colonial Club Baseball Association, we usually play 5 series (Double header on Saturdays) in the fall and attend at least one major tournament in the spring. We also have biweekly practices

name: Beat for Good
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing
description: The purpose of Beat for Good shall be to increase awareness of and support initiatives relating to cardiovascular disease in various communities, including Ithaca, and on Cornell’s campus.

name: BEE Hive Society of Biological and Environmental Engineering
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Engineering
description: The purpose of Hive shall be to create a supportive and informative community for Biological and Environmental Engineering students. We strive to build an environment where students can learn about career paths in their field and the steps that they should take to pursue said fields. We will create interactive and entertaining ways to investigate the BEE major that will excite students.

name: Beef Cattle Club at Cornell

description: The Cornell Bee Club provides opportunities to learn beekeeping in a hands-on setting. Outreach and group collaboration are major goals for the growth of our club.

name: Best Appetizing Bites
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Food/Drink
description: The purpose of Best Appetizing Bites (BaB) shall be to create a community where our members can explore and enjoy Korean food, deepen their understanding of Korean culinary traditions, and foster cultural exchange through discussions around Korean dishes.

name: Beta Alpha Psi
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of Beta Alpha Psi Cornell Chapter shall be to inspire and support excellence by encouraging the study and practice of accounting, finance, business technology, and analytics; providing opportunities for service, professional development, and interaction among members and financial professionals; and fostering lifelong ethical, social, and public responsibilities.

name: Beta Rho Chi
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC)
description: We are a group of individuals driven by a passion for biotechnology and pharmaceuticals in all aspects of industrial, clinical, academic, and entrepreneurial settings. We are a diverse community of researchers, innovators, and creators who share an interest in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and related industries. Since our interests are extremely interdisciplinary, encompassing the fields of medicine, food and nutrition, law and ethics, environmental science, and much more, we welcome students of all majors and backgrounds to be part of the Beta Rho Chi community.

name: Bethany Christian Campus Church
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Spiritual/Religious
description: Bethany Christian Campus Church exists to help students on Cornell campus to grow in their faith

name: Between the Pages
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media
description: The purpose of Between the Pages shall be to create Cornell University's first non-academic book club, focusing on the Young and New Adult genres. Every month, a new book will be chosen and discussed by members, hoping to encourage the diversification of media in the lives of Cornellians.

name: Bhakti Club at Cornell University
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Health/Wellbeing
description: Bhakti is a spiritual thought movement that paves the way for a unique journey of self-discovery. Bhakti Club at Cornell aims to create a space for everyone whether you're seeking answers to life's questions, or searching for a close-knit community. Our goal is to distill the timeless wisdom of spiritual giants and present it in a way that's relevant to today's students. Drawing inspiration from ancient Eastern texts, we use them as a guide to explore a wide range of topics, from science and self-identity to leadership, life management, relationships, and reconnecting with the divine.

name: Bhangra at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Performing Arts
description: Cornell Bhangra's mission is to dance bhangra, engage with and share Punjabi culture, be a supportive network of friends and peers, and give back to our personal, local, and global communities.

name: Big Red Billiards Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Gaming/Esports
description: Join the Ithaca NAPA pool league! This is where most of our players play. Contact Derek Lao or Aodhan Beattie for more information. The game of pocket billiards, or pool as it is commonly known, was massively popular among all groups of people from its inception until the middle of the 20th century. Ever since, it has been on the decline, with fewer and fewer players, reduced prize funds and viewership in major tournaments, and almost complete erasure from American popular culture. Part of the reason is because it has garnered an unsavory reputation due to its association with criminality, gambling, and alcoholism, particularly due to the influence of films like "The Hustler" (1961) and "The Color of Money" (1986). This perception paints an inaccurate and damaging portrait of the pool community, turning away many potential players. Our mission is to foster a lifelong love of the game, as well as to help restore its image and popularity both locally and nationally. To this end, we aim to conduct regular practices and participate in collegiate events to promote the sport's revival.

name: Big Red Heads
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media
description: We showcase the amazing diversity of thought, experiences, and talent in Cornell's community through entertaining, anonymous interviews and student art features.

name: Big Red Raas at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Performing Arts
description: The Cornell Raas Club aims to spread Gujarati culture, in particular the folk dances Raas and Garba, both on and off campus. The club will host workshops to teach the traditional Gujarati dance, attend cultural events, and fund trips to off-campus events.  As a competitive dance team, our purpose is also to teach, practice, and prepare our dancers to preform at competitions nationwide and spread the happiness and joy with which we dance.

name: Big Red Smiles at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing
description: Our mission is to support students passionate about dentistry by fostering an inclusive community and educating members on valuable dentistry/oral health skills, specifically focusing on manual dexterity.

name: Big Red Sports Network (BRSN)
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media
description: Big Red Sports Network (BRSN) is Cornell University's only student-run broadcast media and journalism organization dedicated entirely to Cornell sports. We've grown from two students with a mic to a group 50+ members strong, covering 15+ Men's and Women's sports, and spanning 8 departments. Though we have scaled during our journey, we've stayed true to our mission: meaningfully connecting students, alumni, and fans to Cornell sports and athletes through empowered storytelling: We broadcast for the parent who is unable to travel to watch her daughter compete. We write for the alum who yearns to know today's athletes beyond a box score. And we post for the student who seeks a deeper connection to the Big Red family. But above all else, we evolve to raise the bar because there's nothing else in the world we would rather be doing.

name: Big Red Thon
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, Health/Wellbeing
description: Big Red THON is an independently registered, non-profit organization and Cornell's branch of the Children Miracle Network Hospitals Dance Marathon. We brought the Dance Marathon movement to the Ivy League in 2015, and have raised over $115,000 for Upstate Golisano Children's Hospital in Syracuse. Our yearly Dance Marathon, typically held in Barton Hall, is a celebration of the fundraising campaigns we've held leading up to the main event. BRT works with many on and off campus organizations, our sponsors, and those who help us get one step closer to ending childhood illness. Join Big Red THON today, and join our generation fighting for the next!

name: Big Red Vision
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The mission of Big Red Vision shall be to create a space for pre-optometry students and those interested in pursuing optometry to connect and to feel supported in their endeavors.

name: Big Red Yoga
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The purpose of Big Red Yoga is to create a community for students to practice, learn about, and advocate the 8 limbs of yoga. This will be done by offering the following; hatha yoga lead by certified yoga instructors, yoga book club with discussions on yoga philosophy, specialized workshops, meditative walks in nature, guest lecturers, and member outings to local studios.

name: Bioethics Society at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The mission of the Society for Bioethics at Cornell is to promote modes of thought through the lens of bioethics in the Cornell community in order to facilitate the development of more thoughtful leaders in medicine, science, technology, philosophy, business, and legal/policy oriented professions as they relate to human health.

name: Biological Undergraduate Research Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: To provide undergraduate students with little/no exposure to biology research with basic wet-lab technique experience, assistance with joining labs, and insight into the types of research at Cornell. Members gain teaching and organizational experience and have the opportunity to mentor new students.

This group is open to any and all members of the Cornell University community. No prerequisites necessary, just enthusiasm for birds!

name: Black Architects, Artists, and Planners
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Student Groups for Student Services, AFFILIATION: College of Architecture Art and Planning
description: Black AAP is an opportunity to kickstart a union between Black students, staff and faculty within AAP. The bond between student and teacher is of great importance to the furthering of their knowledge and communication abilities especially amongst Black creators. I hope to contribute greatly towards Cornell University's Architecture, Art and Planning collage by enhancing the comfortability between student, teacher and staff and creating a heightened awareness of people who might look like yourself as a Black person within your department. The hope is also to not only allow Black people with AAP to create connections within the department but it is also to spark something new and exciting for all minorities within AAP. While Black AAP is notable for its inclusion of just Black students, staff and faculty, another distinction lies within its desire to promote relaxation and activity rather than work projects and competitions.

name: Black Ivy Pre-Law Society
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Political/Speech/Debate
description: The Black Ivy Pre-law Society is a professional honor society for students of color who are dedicated to pursuing a degree and career in law upon graduation.

name: Black Lives at Cornell (BLAC) Book
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media
description: The purpose of The BLACBook is to develop community and togetherness among black students and groups on Cornell's campus, as well as to connect with the larger Ithaca black community. The BlacBook seeks to put together a yearbook at the conclusion of each academic year that highlights and shares the experiences of black students, black groups, black events, and so on.

name: Black Student Ensemble
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Performing Arts
description: The purpose of the Black Student Ensemble will be to create a supportive and educational space for women of color to feel represented on campus. With in-depth monthly workshops, which will educate members on black struggles and the social identity of being a woman, we hope to empower giving students the confidence to be themselves.

name: Black Women's Support Network
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: It is the purpose of The Black Women's Support Network to provide a supportive, educational, and social venue where women of African descent can discuss issues affecting and pertaining to their community. Support is consistently provided to these women by giving them ample access to all resources and tools needed to assist them in their academic, personal and social endeavors while at Cornell University. Items under this umbrella include, but are not limited to: academic workshops and development,  sexual/mental/physical/emotional health assistance, and access to other supportive Black women through a variety of social events and initiatives such as the B.O.S.S. (Building Ourselves through Sisterhood and Service), a peer mentorship program for self-identified women of color. Moreover, the Black Women's Support Network aims to serve as a forum where women of color can share, reflect and gain knowledge from each other's experiences. BWSN seeks to accomplish this by providing engaging Sister Circle discussions on a regular basis throughout the year. Sister Circles are our unique form of General Body meetings which occur bi-weekly. The Black Women's Support Network also aims to reach out to other Black women within the Greater Ithaca Community through community service initiatives and interactions with young "at risk" females.

name: BlackGen Capital
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The founding board has set a vision for BlackGen Capital to serve minorities that are underrepresented in the financial services industry and business world. The organization's purpose of most importance is to reduce the barriers that said minorities face when trying to access these fields by cultivating an environment that is not only educating but acts as a platform & network that members can professionally leverage.

name: Blockchain at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell Blockchain Club is based on the belief that the current disconnect between business and technology is both counterintuitive and hindering to the natural progression of society. Overwhelming, the intersection between business and technology, be it in through fintech, the rise of silicon valley, startups, and countless other examples has proven that success in the future requires a concrete understanding of business principles and the utilization of technology, be it through software for analytics optimization of logistics. Cornell Blockchain hopes to further those who are interested technically through its endeavors but also, through education and aspects of blockchain that may not need hands-on technical experience, to help nurture the second phase of adopters. Those of Cornell Blockchain believe that the future lies in blockchain, and thus through the club intend to spread knowledge and mold a standard as blockchain emerges into mass public adoption to become the thought leaders, strategy experts, and technical pioneers in this second phase of adoption.

name: Bowling Club at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The mission of the Bowling Club is to provide Cornell community members of all skill levels with an opportunity to bowl recreationally and/or competitively throughout their college careers. The Bowling Club also provides members with a fun, rewarding, and inclusive community on campus. Disclaimer: this organization is a registered student organization of Cornell University. https://tinyurl.com/Officer-Transition-Doc

name: Boxing Club at Cornell University
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Health/Wellbeing, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The Cornell Boxing Club aims to provide a safe, supportive, and fun environment for any interested student to learn the sport of boxing.

name: Brain Exercise Initiative at Cornell
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: - Brain Exercise Initiative is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit focused on preventing memory loss through brain exercise. - Pioneered by neuroscientist Dr. Ryuta Kawashima, it has been found that doing simple math and reading aloud for just 30 minutes a day, 5 times a week, caused marked improvements for those with Alzheimer's.  Most showed improvements in cognitive function as tested by Mini Mental State Examinations (MMSE) and Frontal Assessment Batteries (FAB). Many began to feel happier and improvements in communication and cognition were recorded.  Near miraculous case studies were also observed. For example, an individual who was previously bedridden began to walk again after completing these exercises for six months. Some patients showed improvements in bowel movement.  The gentle mental activities Dr. Kawashima used activated the prefrontal cortex, the control center for memory, cognition and planning. These activities are currently being done in over 1400 care centers with over 15,000 patients in Japan.  For more information regarding this groundbreaking research done in Japan, please reference these two articles:   https://www.tohoku.ac.jp/en/research/research_highlights/research_highlight_22.html  and https://academic.oup.com/biomedgerontology/article/60/3/380/630607. Drawing from the research conducted in Japan, we are inspired to create an intergenerational nonprofit in which university students would hold brain exercise programs at retirement homes. We creates daily packets which include simple math, writing and "read-alouds" that are completed by each individual with the guidance of university students.  Several retirement homes have integrated the program into their center and chapters are currently being founded at different universities. Not only does the Brain Exercise Initiative hope to improve the memory of those suffering from Alzheimer's but we also create an invaluable, all-too-rare avenue for intergenerational service, discussion, and collaboration.

CYC selects only the most highly qualified undergraduates from America's best universities. Many times there is an acceptance rate of <10% to get into the program. category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: The Cornell BioVentures and Life Sciences Entrepreneurship Club empowers students to turn Cornell’s scientific discoveries into real-world ventures. Partnering with the Center for Life Science Ventures and faculty innovators, we connect undergraduates and graduates with incubator companies, capital networks, and mentorship to accelerate biotech commercialization and cultivate the next generation of life sciences entrepreneurs.

name: Cornell Bitcoin Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Education/Human Services
description: The purpose of the Cornell Bitcoin Club shall be to contribute to fostering a global network of Bitcoin students, promoting education and collaboration and connecting students with opportunities and resources within the Bitcoin ecosystem. As Bitcoin is for every human, so is the Cornell Bitcoin Club.

name: Cornell Brawl Stars Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Gaming/Esports
description: Brawl Stars is a popular mobile game that has been established ever since Dec 12, 2018. However, over the past few years (2024-2026), Brawl Stars saw a large increase in player base. Due to its increasing popularity, making a club where the people at Cornell can play Brawl Stars and find teammates makes sense. It is easily accessible since it is a free mobile game, our organization would allow people who enjoy playing to connect over this shared interest and make friends while also encouraging new players. While Brawl Stars is a game of skill, strategy is also very important for victory, so the club would also be a place where strategies can be exchanged.

name: Cornell Capital Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: (Through our rigorous 10-week new member education process, new members work on two case studies of successful startups. This process provides members with a deep understanding of how to obtain investment, manage finances, develop ideas, and drive company growth. In the final three weeks, students work with teammates to initiate and develop their own projects. Then, they pitch to successful investors associated with Cornell Capital Club, which is an exclusive opportunity available only to Cornell Capital Club members)

name: Cornell Chai Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Food/Drink
description: The mission of the Cornell Chai Club is to provide a platform for students to explore and appreciate the rich cultural traditions of tea from around the world, engage in meaningful discussions, and build lasting connections through shared experiences. We strive to promote relaxation, cultural exchange, and a deeper understanding of the art of tea-making.

name: Cornell Chapter of Partners in Health Engage
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: At Partners in Health, we believe healthcare is a universal human right. Around the world, we fight injustice by providing care first to those who need it most. We are a team of students committed to healthcare equity and community education around the importance of equitable healthcare systems through driven campaigns that build and direct power towards generating new resources, fostering public discourse, and advocating for effective policies that advance health care as a human right. We are fervently dedicated to advocacy for the federal funding and policy needed to support Partners in Health’s work and medical care delivery to underserved communities around the world. As a chapter of the national network of teams of PIH Engage, the organizing sector of Partners in Health with hundreds of chapters nationwide across universities and cities of the US, we draw from our national network of passionate community organizers and policy advocates to advocate for health equity in communities worldwide through local community building, education, and fundraising initiatives that strengthen PIH’s work providing high quality healthcare in the conviction that treatable illnesses should not be a death sentence for those in areas without accessible medical care. Through organizing community education centered events around global public health issues and rights-centered policies that strengthen healthcare infrastructure, we aspire to mobilize the Cornell community around the right to health and justice in public health. Through fundraising for care-delivery programs and community building campaigns around Partners in Health’s work across the calendar year, we strive to emphasize the tremendous impact of a grassroots approach to social justice work in global health, increase participation in health justice issues, and understanding around the importance of equitable access to public health resources in underserved communities both in the US and across the Global South.

name: Cornell Chinese Basketball Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: Provide a platform for all Chinese students, scholars, and faculties who love basketball to foster friendships, enhance sportsmanship, and improve their games

name: Cornell Club Ice Hockey D2
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive
description: Our purpose is to increase the skill level of players dedicated to playing hockey at Cornell so that they may enjoy playing hockey at the collegiate level through a low time commitment. The organization competes at the Division II level of AAU College Hockey and practices twice a week throughout the season. The team may occasionally promote players to the AAU D1 Club Hockey team based on performance and/or need.

name: Cornell Club Rowing
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: We provide an opportunity for all past and new rowers a chance to get back on the water. The goal of the team is to foster discipline, focus, and friendship on and off the water.  We compete in various local regattas through the Cascadilla Boat Club (CBC). As a competitive team, hard work is expected.

name: Cornell Club Waterskiing
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Outdoor Experience
description: Cornell Club Waterskiing was created by a group of undergraduate Cornell students who share a love of being on the water and shredding on the ski! With help from Cornell University as well as some equipment donations from fellow enthusiasts, we hope to spread our love of Waterskiing to the Cornell community and the greater Ithaca area.

name: Cornell Coffee Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Food/Drink
description: Coffee Club is founded on three tenants a.	Education: officers oversee lessons regarding the science, history, politics, economics, and social impact of coffee b.	Outreach: officers communicate with local organizations about opportunities for collaboration c.	Craft: officers oversee education regarding coffee brewing processes

name: Cornell Cognitive Science Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Departmental, Community Service, PROF: Science/Healthcare
description: Our mission is to build community for Cognitive Science majors and students interested in the mind and brain. We explore diverse fields—neuroscience, psychology, computer science, linguistics, philosophy, and more—by hosting social events, academic discussions, creative projects, and community service opportunities.

name: Cornell Commodity Trading Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Johnson College of Business
description: To inform Cornell students about the commodity trading industry as a whole and explore the job opportunities within.

name: Cornell Consulting Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The mission of Cornell Consulting Club is to bring management consulting acumen and industry exposure to students of all levels and all backgrounds. The club has three main purposes: to teach its members the skills and tools fundamental in strategy consulting, to provide students with practical experience by working on projects with local, national and international businesses (and provide clients with top of the line services), and to bridge the gap between its members and the consulting industry through company visits and networking events.

name: Cornell Coptic Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, Spiritual/Religious
description: The mission of establishing a Coptic Club on our college campus is rooted in the desire to create a nurturing and inclusive space for students of the Coptic faith and those interested in learning about it. Our mission is to foster a sense of community among Coptic Orthodox students, helping them strengthen their spiritual journeys, maintain their cultural heritage, and engage with the wider campus community. We aim to promote interfaith dialogue, understanding, and respect while serving as a resource for those seeking knowledge about the Coptic Orthodox tradition. Through our activities, events, and discussions, we aspire to uphold the core values of our faith and share its rich history, spirituality, and traditions with others. This club seeks to be a beacon of faith, culture, and unity, enriching the campus experience for all who join us.

name: Cornell Credit Literacy Student Association
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, Advocacy/Social Justice/Action
description: The Cornell Credit Club aims to enhance students’ understanding of credit scores and personal financial literacy through practical education and peer collaboration. We empower members to build and manage their credit responsibly, develop lifelong financial habits, and gain confidence in navigating the financial systems that shape their futures. By fostering awareness and accessibility, we strive to create a more financially informed Cornell community.

name: Cornell Data Strategy Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The purpose of Cornell Data Strategy Club is to serve as a platform for students interested in merging data science with business consulting and finance.

name: Cornell Entertainment Engineering & Design Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Publication/Media, PROF: Engineering
description: To inspire the next generation of entertainment innovators.

name: Cornell Equity Derivatives Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The Cornell Equity Derivatives Club (CEDC) seeks to educate, empower, and connect students interested in the complex and rapidly evolving world of equity derivatives — including options, futures, and other structured products. Our mission is to bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world application by fostering hands-on learning, professional development, and collaboration within Cornell’s finance community.

name: Cornell Ethics Bowl Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Political/Speech/Debate
description: Our mission as the Cornell Ethics Bowl shall be to foster collaborative discourse around contemporary ethical issues. The APPE "supports and trains the next generation of ethics faculty and professionals, works to improve ethical conduct in our communities and workplaces, and advances public dialogue in ethics and values."

name: Cornell Fanworks Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Gaming/Esports, Visual Arts
description: The Cornell Fanworks Club seeks to provide an open, inclusive, and collaborative space for creating and discussing all types of fanworks including, but not limited to, fanfiction, fanart, fan videos, and cosplay. Creators and consumers of fanworks from all fandoms are welcome and encouraged to participate.

name: Cornell Filipino Student Association
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural
description: 1. To promote and protect the interest of the Filipino community. 2. To promote awareness of Filipino values and culture within the community and CFA. 3. To foster unity and friendship among its members. 4. To promote friendship and cooperation with other organizations and entities.

name: Cornell Financial Analysts Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: CFA is formed with the vision to give students the opportunity to further their education in the finance industry, ultimately being able to secure employment. CFA will expose its members to a proprietary 10-week education series focused on financial services interview preparation, real-world professionals, and programs in order to enhance the learning experience. We welcome and encourage all students at Cornell to join the CFA community. We welcome and encourage all students at Cornell to join the CFA community. CFA will provide support, guidance, and the ability for students to collectively organize learning experiences for all members' interests. Our end goal is to create a platform where upperclassmen can give back to underclassmen that are looking to secure employment within financial services through education and mentorship.

name: Cornell FinTech Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management, PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: The Cornell FinTech Club (CFT) is the first all-encompassing, undergraduate-led fintech club that aims to create spaces and opportunities for students interested in fintech through weekly discussions, continuous education, and events such as hackathons, conferences, and corporate speakers.

name: Cornell Go Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Tabletop Games
description: "The Cornell Go Club is dedicated to promoting the study and enjoyment of the ancient strategic board game Go (also known as Weiqi in Chinese or Baduk in Korean). Our mission is to create a welcoming community where players of all skill levels, from complete beginners to experienced competitors, can learn, play, and appreciate the depth and beauty of the game. We host weekly meetings every Thursday from 7-11pm in Willard Straight Hall, offering friendly matches, teaching sessions, and casual tournaments. The Cornell Go Club aims to foster strategic thinking, cross-cultural understanding, and an enduring appreciation for one of humanity's oldest intellectual arts."

name: Cornell Golf Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Active/Recreational: Competitive, Active/Recreational: Noncompetitive
description: The purpose of the Cornell Club Golf Team is to combine as a unit of competitive golfers in the Cornell community to grow in our appreciation and expertise of the game. The Cornell Golf Team will conform to the uniform system of handicapping and rules set forth by the United States Golf Association. The Club Golf Team will be committed to the traditions and history of the game and compete on a national level as members of the National Collegiate Club Golf Association.

name: Cornell Growth Capital Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The Cornell Growth Capital Club is looking to mentor future generations of leaders in the financial industry specifically those who are looking to enter the field of growth capital. During our new member education process, we will provide hands-on experience through mock portfolios and mentorship to provide a basic understanding of the growth capital and the related fields of private equity, venture capital, credit, and investment banking. In addition, we hope to inspire and provide members with knowledge not only in the growth capital industry, but wherever your career takes them. In true Cornell fashion, the Cornell Growth Capital Club is looking to foster collaboration and empower our members to make positive changes and drive development in the world of growth capital.

name: Cornell Hedge Fund Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - AFFILIATION: Professional Fraternity (PFC), PROF: Business and Management
description: Through real-world investing experience, ongoing education, and mentorship, we seek to provide students with the opportunities to develop their skills and interests in finance, regardless of their background. We are committed to our foundational values of integrity, innovation, and diversity to sustain an atmosphere that maximizes our members' personal and professional growth.

name: Cornell Horn Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Performing Arts
description: To share the beautiful sound of all brass instruments with the Cornell community.

name: Cornell ICPC Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Software/Coding/Programming
description: Cornell ICPC Club is Cornell's official competitive programming team. Every year, we participate in the International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) and organize training sessions to help team members improve their problem-solving and algorithmic thinking skills.

name: Cornell International Finance Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of Cornell International Finance Club shall be to empower students to explore global markets, develop financial expertise, and connect with industry professionals, fostering cross-cultural understanding and preparing members for impactful careers in international finance.

name: Cornell Investments Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of Cornell Investments Club shall be to provide a comprehensive and generalist investment education that covers all facets of the finance industry. Our aim is to equip members with a broad understanding of investment strategies and financial principles, enabling them to navigate the complexities of various financial markets.

name: Cornell Latine Policy Forum
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - Advocacy/Social Justice/Action, Political/Speech/Debate, AFFILIATION: Brooks School
description: The Cornell Latine Policy Forum unites undergraduate, graduate, and Ph.D. students who are dedicated to examining how public policy and administration can advance equity and inclusion for Latine communities. We provide a space for discussion, research, and collaborative learning that connects academic perspectives with the lived experiences of Latine populations across local, national, and global contexts.

name: Cornell Latinos in Business Club
category: Undergrad General Student Organization (GSO) - International/Multicultural, PROF: Business and Management
description: The purpose of Cornell Latinos in Business (CLB) Club shall be to provide Latino students and students interested in LatAm at Cornell University with the necessary resources and opportunities to succeed in a career in business through comprehensive education and community.
